schemaNote: Uses the finding schema specified in the audit brief (id, title, section, type, severity, effort, category, file, line, description, impact, recommendation). AUDIT-001..010 use an older repo-local shape (scope/summary/files/fix). Whoever builds the merged report.html must normalize the ten older files.

findings.title: Automatic subdomain discovery is awaited on the scan critical path with a hardcoded 15s cap, and nothing on screen needs it
findings.description: executeScan starts automatic subdomain discovery at lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:544 and then awaits it at :793. lib/scanner/subdomain-auto.ts:52 caps that work at DEFAULT_AUTO_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000. The clock starts after the target fetch, so total wall clock is fetch + 15s. discoverSubdomainsForRoot (lib/scanner/subdomain-discovery-engine.ts:315) runs four sequential stages: nine passive sources (crt.sh alone has a 15s fetch timeout at :441), a 191-prefix DNS brute force in batches of 50, DNS resolution of up to 1000 passive entries, and HTTP reachability probing of every host at concurrency 25. On a cache miss it cannot finish inside the cap, so it reliably burns the whole 15s. Nobody opts in; it runs on every HTTP scan. The result view does not need it: components/scanner/subdomain-discovery.tsx already renders from initialResult with a click-to-discover fallback, so null is a supported state. Regression introduced at 8e5e11b5 (2026-08-18) with a 10s cap, raised to 15s at a233e0bb (2026-08-19). The same pattern exists at lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:698.
findings.impact: Every scan takes 15-20 seconds instead of 2-5. This is the product's headline speed claim being contradicted on the primary flow, in front of the user, on every single scan. Since commit 3a242f89 the server-reported duration also includes the wait, so the 'Scan duration' stat shows ~17s too. The only surface where the under-3-seconds claim still holds is the landing demo, and only because app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.ts:209 passes cacheOnly: true and skips subdomain discovery, software inventory, CVE enrichment, ports and screenshots entirely.
findings.recommendation: Drop the await at lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:792-796 and the readSubdomains call at :797-802. Let discovery keep running in the background; it already warms the DB cache via subdomain-discovery-engine.ts:418. Have the subdomain panel read that cache lazily. Roughly a 10-line change. Apply the same fix at lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:698. Do this BEFORE removing the timer (scan-05): once the scan actually takes 3s the number stops being a liability and becomes the proof.

findings.title: scan_history.team_id is never written by any scan path, so team scan sharing is dead end to end while shipping a full UI for it
findings.description: PATCH /api/v3/history/[id] destructures teamId at :267, authorizes it at :313-326 and writes it at :349-352. That is the only write path to scan_history.team_id (instrumentation.ts:928) in the entire codebase. Every INSERT INTO scan_history omits the column: app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:368, scan/crawl/route.ts:440, scan/bulk/route.ts:278, scan/authenticated/route.ts:469, scan/github/route.ts:252, lib/scanner/scheduled-scans-worker.ts:280, lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:633. No UI ever sends teamId: the only PATCH bodies sent are {notes} (app/history/page.tsx:394) and {isPublic} (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:339); a repo-wide grep for 'share to team' / 'share with team' across .tsx returns zero. The sibling columns webhooks.team_id (instrumentation.ts:934) and scheduled_scans.team_id (:937) have the same shape: PATCH accepts teamId (webhooks/[id]/route.ts:201, schedules/route.ts:308) and no UI sends it.
findings.impact: GET /api/v3/teams/member-scans queries WHERE user_id = $1 AND team_id = $2 (app/api/v3/teams/member-scans/route.ts:53-60) and can only ever return an empty array, yet the product ships a complete viewer for it with pagination (app/teams/page.tsx:469, components/teams/team-member-scans.tsx). Every getTeamResourceAccess team branch across history, share and report is unreachable. The feature is documented and sold at app/docs/teams/page.tsx:374-380. A paying team customer sees an empty panel with no explanation.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Share with team' control to components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx beside the existing 'Make private' item at :590, populated from getAssignableTeamIds with a 'Personal (private)' null option, plus a team column and filter on History. Add the same selector to the webhook and schedule rows on Profile > Developer. Alternatively decide the feature is not wanted and remove the columns, the read paths and the docs section.

findings.title: The 'send the verification email again' button is dead: it checks a success field the API envelope never sets
findings.description: The handler branches on `if (res.ok && data.success)` then `else if (!res.ok)`. lib/api/api-utils.ts:15 defines ApiResponse.success as `NextResponse.json(data, { status })`, which adds no success field. app/api/v3/auth/resend-verification/route.ts returns ApiResponse.success({ message: ... }) at lines 44, 54 and 64, so the body is a bare {message}. On a 200 response data.success is undefined, so the first branch is false and `!res.ok` is also false. Neither branch executes. components/auth/signup-success.tsx:45 and components/auth/verify-email-expired.tsx:46 check res.ok alone and work correctly.
findings.impact: An unverified user is told to check their email, clicks 'send again', watches the button spin and reset, and sees nothing change. They click repeatedly until the rate limit trips, at which point they finally get an error, which reads as the resend being broken rather than throttled. This is the terminal step of the signup funnel.
findings.recommendation: Delete `&& data.success` from the condition at components/auth/login-form.tsx:54. Match the two sibling components that already do this correctly.

findings.title: /profile is the last page on the retired horizontal icon strip, and below 640px it has no accessible name on any tab
findings.description: app/profile/page.tsx:722-741 is inline JSX rendering eight buttons, each `{tab.icon}` plus `{tab.label}`. The replacement components are AdminMobileSectionTrigger and AdminMobileToc (components/admin/shared/admin-mobile-toc.tsx:68 and :123), consumed at app/admin/page.tsx:1034-1057, whose own docstring at :59-62 reads 'Lives at the top of the mobile sidebar in place of the old horizontal icon strip.' The docs equivalent is DocsMobileNavTrigger / DocsMobileNav (components/docs/docs-mobile-nav.tsx:19 and :43). Four defects verified: (1) lucide auto-applies aria-hidden="true" when a component carries no a11y prop (node_modules/lucide-react/dist/cjs/lucide-react.js:92) and the TABS array at :625-664 passes none, so at 375px each button holds one aria-hidden SVG plus one display:none span; (2) eight buttons at px-3.5 plus a 16px icon is 44px each, 366px against 343px available, and scrollbar-hide (app/globals.css:37) removes the only signal that the row scrolls; (3) the strip is lg:hidden, so between 640px and 1023px labels return and it grows to ~910px against 736px, hiding two tabs; (4) missing type="button" and aria-current, both of which the new pattern supplies at admin-mobile-toc.tsx:187,190.
findings.impact: On a phone, account settings navigation is eight unlabeled icons with one cut in half and no indication the row scrolls. A screen reader announces 'button' eight times with no way to distinguish them, so a screen-reader user cannot navigate /profile at all.
findings.recommendation: Replace lines 722-741 with AdminMobileSectionTrigger plus AdminMobileToc, passing the eight TABS entries as AdminTocItem[] with active and onSelect, grouped the way app/admin/page.tsx:997-1009 builds mobileSectionItems from NAV_GROUPS. Note that /profile's own Developer sub-tabs at components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:663-696 are already the correct version of this strip (labels never hidden, type="button", aria-current, explicit aria-hidden) - the page header is an older, worse copy of its own child.

findings.title: Admin row actions including Delete are invisible on touch but still hit-testable, in four list panels
findings.description: Four panels use `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` as the only rendering condition for their row action buttons: components/admin/notifications/notifications-manager.tsx:625, components/admin/features/mass-email-manager.tsx:573, components/admin/features/security-alerts-manager.tsx:367 and :382, and components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:1834. Touch devices have no hover state, so the buttons are permanently invisible while remaining fully hit-testable. Six sibling admin panels pair `hidden md:block` with an `md:hidden` card list; these four did not. The same class of bug exists at components/teams/team-members-list.tsx:146, where the member kebab (View Scans / Remove) has no sm: prefix, while components/shares/shares-row.tsx:118 does it correctly with `sm:opacity-0 sm:group-hover:opacity-100 sm:group-focus-within:opacity-100`.
findings.impact: An admin on a phone cannot see row actions at all, and can fire a destructive one, including Delete, by tapping apparently blank space.
findings.recommendation: Change to `md:opacity-0 md:group-hover:opacity-100` in all four admin panels so the actions are unconditionally visible below md. Bring components/teams/team-members-list.tsx:146 in line with components/shares/shares-row.tsx:118.

findings.title: The findings toolbar overflows the viewport and horizontally scrolls the whole page, which is what makes /history read as broken on mobile
findings.description: components/scanner/results-list.tsx:398 is `<div className="flex items-center gap-2">` with no flex-wrap and no overflow wrapper, containing three buttons each marked shrink-0 at :408, :425 and :448. Measured: 'Most severe first' about 146px, 'Group by severity' about 146px, 'Select' about 82px, plus two gap-2 gaps, totalling roughly 390px. Content width on /history is 375 - 32 = 343px (app/history/page.tsx:443, max-w-6xl mx-auto px-4). No ancestor has overflow-x-hidden, so the row spills into body. The reason this reads as a /history-specific bug is that the 'Select' button only renders when selectable = Boolean(scanUrl) (:126), which is set only on the two owner surfaces, /history and /dashboard. On /shared, /host and /demo the row is about 300px and fits. /demo is additionally immune because components/demo/demo-shell.tsx:9 carries overflow-x-hidden.
findings.impact: The entire page scrolls sideways on any phone. This is the single most visible mobile defect in the product and the one the owner reported.
findings.recommendation: Change line 398 to `flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2` and drop shrink-0 from lines 408, 425 and 448. Alternatively keep one row and wrap each label in `<span className="hidden sm:inline">`, leaving the icons.

findings.title: Checkout reads meData.data on an endpoint that returns flat, so every existing subscriber gets the wrong upgrade flow
findings.description: app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:60-66 reads `meData.data?.subscriptionStatus` and `meData.data?.role`. app/api/v3/auth/me/route.ts returns ApiResponse.success({...}) at lines 47 and 133, and lib/api/api-utils.ts:15 confirms ApiResponse.success returns the object flat with no data wrapper. So meData.data is undefined and both reads are permanently undefined.
findings.impact: hasActiveSubscription is permanently false, so an existing subscriber upgrading is shown the full card-entry form instead of SwitchPlanPanel. They type card details that the server action then ignores, because it prorates against the card already on file. A large share will abandon the flow believing they are about to be charged twice. isStaffAccount is likewise permanently false, making the staff guard at :96-114 dead code. This is on the money path.
findings.recommendation: Drop the .data hop: use meData?.subscriptionStatus and meData?.role.

findings.title: A domain with no discoverable subdomains pays the full 15s penalty on every scan forever, because an empty cache result is treated as a miss
findings.description: getCachedSubdomainSnapshot returns a snapshot whose subdomains array can be empty; the guard `if (!row?.subdomains) return null` passes a truthy [] through, and the caller in lib/scanner/subdomain-auto.ts gates the cache hit on `cached.subdomains.length > 0`. An empty-but-fresh cache row therefore reads as a miss and re-runs the full 15s discovery. Compounding this, SUBDOMAIN_CACHE_TTL_HOURS is only 4 (lib/config/config-values.ts:582), so even successful cache entries expire quickly.
findings.impact: Any domain that genuinely has no discoverable subdomains, which is the common case for a personal site or a single-host deployment, pays the maximum penalty on every scan indefinitely and never benefits from the cache at all.
findings.recommendation: Change the cache-hit gate from `cached.subdomains.length > 0` to 'a fresh cache row exists at all', and raise SUBDOMAIN_CACHE_TTL_HOURS from 4. Note this only helps repeat scans; the first scan of any domain still pays the full cost until scan-01 is fixed.

findings.title: The scanning page timer undersells the engine and should be removed once the latency is fixed
findings.description: components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx:118 starts a pure client stopwatch with useState(() => Date.now()), ticked at :149 and rendered at :271-273. It starts at setStatus('scanning') in app/dashboard/page.tsx:471, before the POST at :537, and stops only when React unmounts the indicator at :910. It floors the value (:77-81), so a displayed '17s' means at least 17.0 real seconds. Separately, the server-reported 'Scan duration' stat (components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:303-310, from result.duration, snapshotted at lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:823) also includes the subdomain wait since commit 3a242f89. Both numbers are honest and both show roughly 17s. The 2-5s engine time is not surfaced anywhere in the product. Verified NOT the cause: there is no artificial minimum display time (the cosmetic timers at :42, :58, :69 cannot hold the flip because the component is unmounted by the status conditional), no serial post-completion fetches, and no router.refresh().
findings.impact: The product's core differentiator is speed, and the only number the user watches contradicts it on every scan.
findings.recommendation: Fix scan-01 first. Then replace the elapsed-seconds readout with progress that carries information rather than a number that invites comparison: the check family currently running, the count of checks completed against the total, and the findings counter ticking up as they land. If a duration is shown at all after the fix, show the server-reported engine time and label it as such.

findings.title: The 'Skip to main content' link is dead on roughly 790 pages, and it makes two published accessibility claims false
findings.description: app/layout.tsx:172 renders one skip link for the whole app targeting #main-content. Three of the four public shells never render that target: components/shared/public-page-shell.tsx:60 has no id and no tabIndex; lib/seo/seo-ui.tsx:19 is a bare `<main className="flex-1">`; components/docs/docs-shell.tsx:77 uses an orphan id="docs-content" that no anchor anywhere references. components/legal/legal-shell.tsx:15 is the one that gets it right. Blast radius: public-page-shell covers /changelog, /compare, /contact, /security, /host/[hostname], /public-scans, /shared/[token] (7 routes); lib/seo/seo-ui.tsx covers /checks plus ~754 generated /checks/[id] pages plus 18 category pages, /alternatives plus ~5 competitor pages, /tools and its two children (~780 routes); docs-shell covers ~20 docs routes.
findings.impact: A keyboard or screen-reader user pressing Tab on any of those pages gets a visible, focusable skip link that jumps nowhere. It also makes two statements in the published accessibility statement false: app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:92-95 claims 'Skip navigation links allow users to bypass repetitive content', and :89-90 claims 'All form inputs have associated labels for clarity' (contradicted by docs-07). That moves this from an accessibility bug to a legal-accuracy one.
findings.recommendation: Three one-line changes matching components/legal/legal-shell.tsx:15: set id="main-content" tabIndex={-1} on components/docs/docs-shell.tsx:77, lib/seo/seo-ui.tsx:19 and components/shared/public-page-shell.tsx:60. tabIndex={-1} is required for the target to actually receive focus.

findings.title: The cookie notice paints over every floating save bar, making /profile and two admin editors unsaveable on mobile
findings.description: components/shared/cookie-notice.tsx:47 is `fixed inset-x-0 bottom-0 z-50` and is mounted last in app/layout.tsx:194, after TosGate and its children. Three floating save bars are also z-50 and are rendered inside children: app/profile/page.tsx:929, components/admin/features/system-settings-manager.tsx:664 and components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:2731. At equal z-index the later paint wins, so the notice covers all three. At 375px the notice is flex-col with a roughly three-line paragraph plus py-3 plus an h-8 button row, about 125px tall, while the save card sits at y16-72px. It shows for every visitor who has not dismissed it (localStorage key vr-cookie-notice-dismissed).
findings.impact: The 'Save Changes' button is completely unreachable on /profile, on admin System Settings and on the admin user detail panel until the notice is dismissed. On desktop the notice is about 52px tall so the buttons are only partially covered.
findings.recommendation: Raise the notice to z-60 and have it publish its height as --vr-cookie-h the way components/shared/site-notifications.tsx:586 publishes --vr-banner-h, then offset the save bars by bottom-[calc(var(--vr-cookie-h,0px))]. While there, extract the three duplicated save bars into components/shared/floating-save-bar.tsx beside the existing components/shared/save-confirmation-modal.tsx.

findings.title: The cookie notice also buries the docs 'Contents' FAB, which is the only route to docs navigation below lg
findings.description: The same roughly 125px cookie-notice band at 375px swallows the docs Contents FAB at components/docs/docs-mobile-nav.tsx:26, which sits at bottom-20 occupying the 80-120px band. Below lg that FAB is the only route to the docs sidebar and the on-page table of contents.
findings.impact: A visitor arriving on /docs/api from a search result on a phone has no navigation at all until they notice and dismiss the cookie bar.
findings.recommendation: Once the notice publishes --vr-cookie-h (see shell-02), set the FAB to bottom-[calc(5rem+var(--vr-cookie-h,0px))].

findings.title: The AI chat launcher covers the Save Changes button on /profile and the bottom-right of every commerce form
findings.description: components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:1613-1617 renders a 56px FAB at bottom-5 right-5 z-50, mounted after children. Its route gating at :1273-1284 returns null on /browser/, /docs and /admin, but not /profile. At 375px the save card spans to right:16px with right-aligned buttons, so the FAB occupying right 20-76px and y 20-76px sits directly over Save Changes.
findings.impact: Compounds shell-02 on /profile: even after dismissing the cookie notice, the chat launcher still covers the save button on a phone. Also covers the bottom-right of forms on /pricing, /checkout, /contact, /legal and the auth pages.
findings.recommendation: Offset the launcher by --vr-cookie-h and give the floating save bars right padding that clears 76px on mobile, or add /profile to the launcher's null-return route list.

findings.title: A failed history fetch renders the 'no scans yet' empty state, so a server error looks like data loss
findings.description: app/history/page.tsx:222-236 fetches API.HISTORY and, on a non-ok response, redirects only for 401 and 403 and otherwise returns early. scans stays [] and loading goes false, so HistoryEmptyState (components/history/history-empty-state.tsx:23-43) renders 'No scans recorded yet. Run your first scan.' Any 500, gateway error or non-JSON body produces this. The same pattern exists at app/assets/page.tsx:68-84, app/badge/page.tsx:29-42, and app/shares/page.tsx:76-89, which does not check status at all so even a 401 renders SharesEmptyState.
findings.impact: A user with 200 scans is told they have none. That reads as data loss, which is the single worst thing a security tool can appear to do, and it will generate support tickets and churn.
findings.recommendation: Add an error state to each of the four pages and render a distinct 'Couldn't load your history. Retry.' block instead of the empty state. The distinction between 'empty' and 'failed to load' must be visible in every list view.

findings.title: The teammate scan 'View' button links to a hash the history page never reads, using the wrong id
findings.description: components/teams/team-member-scans.tsx:107 renders `<a href={`/history#${scan.id}`}>`. /history reads only ?scan=<public_id> (app/history/page.tsx:161,176-178) and nothing anywhere reads location.hash. Compounding this, MemberScan.id is the numeric primary key (components/teams/teams-types.ts:47), not the opaque public_id the route resolves.
findings.impact: Clicking View drops the user on the unfiltered history list with no indication of what happened. Both halves are wrong, so even adding hash handling would not fix it.
findings.recommendation: Return public_id from /api/v3/teams/member-scans and link to `/history?scan=${scan.publicId}`.

findings.title: Teammate scan panel can display one member's scans under another member's name
findings.description: app/teams/page.tsx:459-481 sets viewingMember unconditionally at :464 and only assigns memberScans inside the `if (res.ok)` branch at :472. memberScans is never cleared. After a successful load for member A, a failed load for member B leaves A's scan list in state while the heading renders `{member.name}'s Scan History` (components/teams/team-member-scans.tsx:45). The memberScansReqRef ticket guards response ordering but not the error path, which is the same class of mislabel it was written to prevent.
findings.impact: One teammate's scanned URLs are displayed under a different teammate's name. On a team feature this is a trust and privacy problem, not just a rendering bug.
findings.recommendation: Call setMemberScans([]) before the fetch and add an explicit error branch that renders a failure state rather than leaving stale data on screen.

findings.title: Avatar upload failure sets an undefined error, so the toast never renders and the upload fails with zero feedback
findings.description: app/profile/page.tsx:164 does `setError(data.error)` with no fallback string, unlike every sibling save path in the same file (`data.error || "Failed to update your name."` at about :416, `|| "Failed to update your email."` at about :432). A non-2xx body without an error key sets undefined. The toast condition at :687 is `{(error || success) && ...}`, which is falsy, so nothing renders. The spinner stops via the finally at :179 and the crop dialog stays open.
findings.impact: The upload fails silently and the user retries the same failing file indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: setError(data.error || "Failed to upload profile picture.")

findings.title: Six billing components render raw server-action error messages, which in production is Next.js boilerplate about omitted messages
findings.description: app/actions/stripe.ts:1 is "use server", and Next 15.5.23 (package.json:95) redacts thrown server-action errors in production builds. So err.message on the client is the framework boilerplate 'An error occurred in the Server Components render. The specific message is omitted in production builds to avoid leaking sensitive details. A digest property is included...'. Six sites render it verbatim into a user-facing toast: components/profile/tabs/profile-billing-tab.tsx:143, components/billing/ai-credit-checkout.tsx:235, components/billing/browserbase-credit-checkout.tsx:230, components/billing/github-credit-checkout.tsx:228, components/billing/stripe-checkout.tsx:214 and :344.
findings.impact: A user whose payment or portal action fails is shown a paragraph of React internals instead of an explanation. On the billing surface specifically this reads as the product being broken with their money involved.
findings.recommendation: Always use the fallback string rather than err.message, or convert the server actions to return {ok: false, error} instead of throwing.

findings.title: /compare fails silently and permanently on every error, with an explicitly no-op catch
findings.description: app/compare/page.tsx:54-64 fetches the compare endpoint, sets diffResult only `if (res.ok)`, has no else branch, and catches with `/* ignore */`. A 403 (a shared link to someone else's scans), a 404 (deleted scan), a 500 or a dropped connection all land identically: loading flips false, diffResult stays null, and the UI re-renders the scan picker with the Compare button live again. app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:238-240 already has the correct pattern in-repo.
findings.impact: The user clicks Compare, watches a spinner, and is returned exactly where they started with no explanation. Clicking again reproduces it forever. A shared /compare link the recipient cannot access shows the generic host picker with no hint why.
findings.recommendation: Add an error state set in both the non-ok branch and the catch, rendered above the Compare button.

findings.title: 2FA 'start over' traps the user in a form that then submits a null userId forever
findings.description: app/login/page.tsx:109 initialises needs2FA with useState(isThirdPartyPending2FA), a one-time initial value rather than derived state. The reset action calls router.push("/login"), a same-route soft navigation, so the component never remounts and the initial value is never recomputed.
findings.impact: The URL changes but the 2FA form stays mounted and now submits userId: null on every attempt, permanently. The user cannot reach the login form again without a hard reload they have no reason to attempt.
findings.recommendation: Derive needs2FA from the current search params on each render, or use window.location.assign("/login") to force a remount.

findings.title: An expired verification link renders 'that link did not verify anything', and the only resend form is unreachable dead code
findings.description: app/verify-email/VerifyEmailClient.tsx:57 branches on `if (data.expired)`, but a repo-wide grep for 'expired: true' returns zero hits and the route sends a plain 400 for an expired token. Expiry therefore falls through to VerifyEmailError. components/auth/verify-email-expired.tsx is 152 lines and is the only screen carrying an inline resend form; no user can reach it.
findings.impact: The user is told their link was invalid rather than merely stale, and is routed toward the dead resend button in auth-01. Two failures compound on the same flow.
findings.recommendation: Have the route return {expired: true} on token expiry, or branch on the 400's error code client-side, so components/auth/verify-email-expired.tsx becomes reachable.

findings.title: Five real OAuth error codes render an empty string, so a failed Discord sign-in shows a normal login form
findings.description: The ?error= mapper at app/login/page.tsx:47-89 has no catch-all and ends in `return ""`. Five codes the OAuth callback actually emits are unmapped: discord_invalid, discord_not_configured, discord_invalid_state, discord_user_failed, session_expired.
findings.impact: A Discord sign-in that fails for any of these reasons bounces the user back to a login form that looks completely normal, with no message at all. They retry and fail identically, with no path to understanding why.
findings.recommendation: Add a catch-all before `return ""`, for example 'Sign-in failed. Try again, or use another method.'

findings.title: The unsubscribe page reports success on failure, which is a compliance exposure
findings.description: app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:214 never checks res.ok and catches with /* ignore */, so a 404 'Invalid token.' still renders the green 'Saved.' confirmation. The unsubscribe-from-all path at :249 has no else branch at all.
findings.impact: The user toggles off Product Updates, is told it saved, and keeps receiving mail. On an unsubscribe screen specifically a false success is a compliance exposure, not merely a UX bug.
findings.recommendation: Check res.ok, render data.error or a fallback in the existing message slot, and never set the success state on a non-2xx response.

findings.title: Turnstile has no failure path, so a user who cannot reach Cloudflare can neither sign up nor contact support
findings.description: components/shared/turnstile-widget.tsx:67 registers no error-callback, no timeout and no failure state. If challenges.cloudflare.com is blocked by a corporate proxy, an ad blocker, a regional block or a Cloudflare outage, the widget stays an empty div forever and the gated submit button stays greyed with no explanation. Gated consumers: components/auth/signup-form.tsx:244, components/contact/contact-form.tsx:346, components/contact/support-tickets.tsx:406.
findings.impact: A user who cannot reach Cloudflare cannot create an account, and cannot use the contact form to report that they cannot create an account. Both exits are behind the same widget.
findings.recommendation: Wire error-callback and a roughly 10 second timeout to a state that renders 'Verification could not load. Refresh, or contact us at {SUPPORT_EMAIL}.' and either enables the submit or offers a fallback route.

findings.title: The blocked-data security panel shows a green all-clear when its fetch fails
findings.description: components/admin/features/blocked-data-manager.tsx:99 and :125 do not check res.ok, so a 403 or 500 yields [] and the panel renders a green CheckCircle2 'No blocked rules'. Both sibling panels, components/admin/features/ip-rules-manager.tsx:91 and security-alerts-manager.tsx:101, carry a comment explaining this exact fix; this file was missed.
findings.impact: An admin reads a security panel as clean when it simply failed to load. That is worse than an error, because it actively asserts a false negative on a security surface.
findings.recommendation: Copy the sibling guard and render an error state visually distinct from the empty state.

findings.title: Admin 'Save as Draft' fails silently and the composed mass email is lost
findings.description: components/admin/features/mass-email-manager.tsx:136 is `if (res.ok) {...}` with no else branch, and the file contains no toast surface at all.
findings.impact: An admin composes a mass email, clicks Save as Draft, and the work is gone with no warning.
findings.recommendation: Add the shared components/admin/shared/toast.tsx and an error branch.

findings.title: Teams cannot be renamed from a phone because the rename affordance exists only in the desktop branch
findings.description:
setEditingTeam is only read by the desktop cell inside `hidden md:block`; the md:hidden mobile card renders the team name as a plain

.
findings.impact: An admin on a phone has no way to rename a team.
findings.recommendation: Add the rename affordance to the md:hidden card branch.

findings.title: The admin Teams page-size selector is wired to state the fetch ignores
findings.description: components/admin/teams/teams-list.tsx:648-652 renders PaginationControl with onPageSizeChange, which sets teamsPageSize (app/admin/page.tsx:227), but fetchTeams at app/admin/page.tsx:347 hardcodes limit: "10" and never reads it. The backend supports up to 100 (app/api/v3/admin/teams/route.ts:29-32).
findings.impact: Selecting 50 highlights the button and still returns 10 rows. A control that visibly responds while changing nothing is worse than no control.
findings.recommendation: Pass String(teamsPageSize) and add it to the dependency array.

findings.title: The engine-feedback modal has no height cap, so its primary action is clipped off-screen with no scroll container
findings.description: Every other hand-rolled admin modal sets max-h-[80vh] overflow-y-auto; components/admin/features/engine-feedback-manager.tsx:836 sets neither.
findings.impact: On a short viewport the 'Promote to Rule' button, the modal's entire purpose, is clipped with no way to scroll to it.
findings.recommendation: Add max-h-[80vh] overflow-y-auto, or migrate to components/ui/dialog.tsx which already supplies it at :39.

findings.title: Four admin panels ship raw desktop tables to phones while six siblings have a card fallback
findings.description: components/admin/features/engine-feedback-manager.tsx:374 (eight columns), components/admin/features/blocked-data-manager.tsx:563, components/admin/features/content-manager.tsx:334 and components/admin/features/billing-overview-manager.tsx:238 render only a desktop table. Six sibling panels pair `hidden md:block` with an `md:hidden` card list. They do not cause page-level horizontal scroll because components/ui/table.tsx:9 wraps every table in overflow-auto, but each scrolls independently inside a viewport too narrow to read it.
findings.impact: Four admin surfaces are effectively unusable on a phone.
findings.recommendation: Add the md:hidden card branch the six sibling panels already implement.

findings.title: The monthly to yearly upgrade has no entry point because the current-plan check ignores billing interval
findings.description: components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:124 is `const isCurrentPlan = currentPlan === plan.id;`, which ignores the billing interval. Flipping the hero's -20% monthly/yearly toggle still renders a disabled 'Current Plan' button for a user on the monthly tier.
findings.impact: /checkout/pro_supporter_yearly is reachable only by typing the URL, even though app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:199 already ships 'Switch to yearly billing' copy for it. The 20 percent annual upsell has no entry point anywhere in the product.
findings.recommendation: Compare the billing interval as well as the plan id.

findings.title: 'Go to the dashboard now' does not navigate, stranding the user on a success screen during a slow confirmation
findings.description: components/billing/stripe-checkout.tsx:121 calls onSuccess(), which renders the 'You are subscribed' screen while confirmation is still retrying, and never navigates anywhere. The three credit components use a real <Link>.
findings.impact: The user clicks the escape hatch during a slow confirmation and is left on a success screen for a subscription that may not have confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Use <Link href={ROUTES.DASHBOARD}> as the three sibling components do.

findings.title: The findings bulk-remediation toolbar is the only true bulk action in the product, and it is poor enough to justify removal
findings.description: Select mode lives at components/scanner/results-list.tsx:122-226 with the toggle at :440-458, the row checkbox at :659-669 and the bulk bar at :685-770. It is gated by scanUrl from canRemediate (components/scanner/scan-result-detail.tsx:71-74) so it appears only on /dashboard after a scan and on /history?id=n. Four specific problems: (1) in select mode the row body is still a full-width button that navigates (:811-813), and opening a finding unmounts ResultsList entirely (its own comment at :228-234 says so) while selected, selectMode and overlay are all local useState, so one mis-tap on row 38 of 200 wipes the selection with no persistence anywhere; (2) selection ignores filters silently, so narrowing the severity filter leaves hidden picks selected and Apply hits findings the user cannot see; (3) at 360px the bar wraps to three rows, roughly 130-160px, a quarter of the viewport, pinned over the list being selected from, one of those rows being a cramped native date picker; (4) the backend is a bulk endpoint in name only, fanning out to Promise.all of up to 200 independent pool.query calls with no transaction (app/api/v3/scan/remediation/bulk/route.ts:83-119), so partial failure leaves partial state behind a generic 'Couldn't apply. Try again.' There is no select-all, no per-group select, no shift-click range, no keyboard toggle (shiftKey appears nowhere in the repo), no confirmation and no undo, and status 'open' deletes each row including notes and assignees irreversibly.
findings.impact: The one place multi-select carries real weight, triaging the 100+ findings a crawl scan produces, is the place it works worst. Users lose selections to mis-taps and cannot tell which findings an Apply actually touched.
findings.recommendation: Owner's call, and both paths are costed. REMOVE is roughly 565 lines: results-list.tsx ~235 (893 to ~660), the route 128, its tests 111, openapi-spec.ts ~35, docs/triage ~40, docs-knowledge.md ~15, plus one line each in client-constants.ts:226, scan-result-detail.tsx, dashboard-results.tsx:232 and history/page.tsx:499. useTeammates survives (issue-detail.tsx:296 also uses it) and the per-finding RemediationControl remains as the fallback. REDESIGN is roughly two days: delete the mode toggle and make the row's left severity bar a 36px selection target; lift selection into lib/hooks/use-finding-selection.ts backed by sessionStorage keyed on scanUrl so it survives navigation; add tri-state select-all on the count line and on each severity group header; collapse the toolbar to '[N selected] [Mark as v] [Clear]' on desktop and a full-width action sheet of five 44px rows on mobile; add x to toggle, shift-click to extend, Esc to clear; replace confirmation with an 8-second Undo, which requires capturing prior remediation rows and giving the route an items[] body shape; and replace the Promise.all fan-out with one INSERT ... SELECT ... FROM unnest(...) inside a transaction so the all-or-nothing error copy becomes honest.

findings.title: Share-link expiry is fully implemented, enforced on every read path, and unreachable from the UI
findings.description: The route accepts expiresInDays constrained to 7, 30, 90 or null (app/api/v3/history/[id]/share/route.ts:12, :21-32, :110-113, :142) and scan_history.share_expires_at (instrumentation.ts:1307) is enforced on every read path: app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:35, public-scans/route.ts:75, shares/route.ts:27. A repo-wide grep for expiresInDays outside app/api returns zero hits, and the share action POSTs no body at all (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:290). The Shares page already renders the expiry via formatExpiry (components/shares/shares-types.ts:34, called at components/shares/shares-row.tsx:114), so it permanently prints 'Never expires' for every row.
findings.impact: Every share link ever created is unlimited. A user who shares a scan with a contractor or a client has no way to time-limit it, on a feature where time-limiting is the main security control. The UI already has a slot showing the value it can never set.
findings.recommendation: Add an expiry select (Never / 7 days / 30 days / 90 days) to components/scanner/share-modal.tsx beside the existing publiclyListed switch at :135, and a 'Change expiry' item to the row menu on app/shares/page.tsx. Note drift-15 first: publiclyListed on POST is currently ignored for an existing live share, which will bite whoever adds expiry to the same request.

findings.title: A deep (crawl) scan silently discards the user's scanner and active-probe selection
findings.description: app/dashboard/page.tsx:414-449 destructures scanners from the form payload but stores only pendingCrawlUrl, pendingIsPublic, pendingScreenshot and pendingPortScan (state declared :245-253); there is no pendingScanners. handleCrawlConfirm at :711-724 then passes undefined as the categoryFilter argument. app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:202-205 accepts scanners perfectly well, and the extension does send them, so this is purely a dashboard state bug.
findings.impact: On any deep scan, unchecking check families or ticking active probes has no effect at all. The user configures the scan, watches it run, and gets results that ignore the configuration, with no indication anything was dropped.
findings.recommendation: Add pendingScanners to the pending-crawl state alongside the four existing fields and pass it through handleCrawlConfirm.

findings.title: The extension sends a probes array on every scan that no server handler reads, so its entire Service Probes panel is a no-op
findings.description: extension/src/lib/scan.ts:220-231 serialises the user's Service Probes settings as an array like ["ssh:22", "smtp:587"] into the POST body for both /api/v3/scan and /api/v3/scan/crawl. No handler reads it, verified against app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:232-243 (which reads url, scanners, isPublic, captureScreenshot, portScan only), crawl/route.ts:199-217, authenticated/route.ts:115-129, bulk/route.ts:457, and both execute-scan.ts and execute-crawl-scan.ts. The web app runs its probes as active-probes:<id> entries inside scanners (components/scanner/scan-form.tsx:474-489), an entirely different mechanism. The extension's options panel (extension/src/options/options.ts:238, config at extension/src/lib/types.ts:298) writes settings that go nowhere.
findings.impact: An extension user configures service probes, saves, scans, and nothing happens. It is also still documented as live in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:706-710 and described to users by the AI assistant via lib/ai/system-prompt.ts:234,239, so the product actively tells people a dead feature works.
findings.recommendation: Either translate the extension's probes array into the scanners active-probes:<id> form the server actually understands, or remove the panel, the type, the OpenAPI block and the system-prompt lines together.

findings.title: The admin 'set scan limit' action writes a column no limiter reads, and the AI assistant repeats the fake number to users
findings.description: app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:1523-1542 writes users.daily_scan_limit (instrumentation.ts:304) with a value from 0 to 10000 and audit-logs 'Set daily scan limit to N'. getDailyLimit() at lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts:112-147 resolves the cap purely from getUserPlan() to a BILLING_* setting and never reads the column. Its only readers are the AI chat context (app/api/v3/ai/chat/route.ts:156, ai/context/route.ts:261, lib/ai/system-prompt.ts:94) and the GDPR export (data-request/route.ts:129). The action itself has no UI dispatch either; it appears in components/admin/config.ts only as an audit-log label.
findings.impact: An admin action reports success, writes an audit row asserting the change, and enforces nothing. Worse, the AI assistant reads that column and confidently quotes a daily limit to the user that the system does not apply.
findings.recommendation: Decide one way: either make getDailyLimit honour a non-null override, or delete the action, the column and the AI/export readers. Do not add a UI control before resolving this.

findings.title: POST /api/v3/scan/bulk is fully built and has no UI caller; the dashboard loops single scans instead
findings.description: app/api/v3/scan/bulk/route.ts is 734 lines and accepts {urls[], isPublic}, scanning up to a plan-capped 100 URLs in one request. API.SCAN_BULK is declared at lib/config/constants.ts:747 and referenced by nothing outside the docs pages and landing-api-example.tsx:118. The dashboard's bulk panel instead loops POST /api/v3/scan one URL at a time at app/dashboard/page.tsx:743-775, and detects rate limits by string-matching error text at :762-763. The two paths have separately-audited quota and privacy handling. Note also that FEATURE_BULK_SCANS gates only the unused public endpoint (scan/bulk/route.ts:346), so disabling the flag does not disable the dashboard's bulk tab.
findings.impact: The first-party UI pays N round trips for what the server does in one, repeatedly trips its own burst limiter, reports failure per URL instead of atomically, and diverges from the audited code path. Bulk scanning is a sold plan feature priced 5/10/25/100 across tiers.
findings.recommendation: Point handleBulkScan at API.SCAN_BULK with the whole array. Roughly 40 lines out of app/dashboard/page.tsx replaced by about 15, and the feature flag starts working.

findings.title: Twenty-eight build-tier admin settings write rows nothing ever reads, including the checks-count label used across marketing surfaces
findings.description: Twenty-eight registry keys are marked build tier with field help saying an edit 'applies on the next build', but no build-time system_settings reader exists: prebuild (package.json:13) only compiles knowledge files, and next build compiles the config-values.ts literals. Verified consumers bypass the setting entirely, for example MAX_AVATAR_UPLOAD_BYTES read at lib/uploads/avatar.ts:24 and components/profile/tabs/profile-general-tab.tsx:74, and TOTAL_CHECKS_LABEL read at app/api/v3/ai/context/route.ts:94 and app/landing/page.tsx:31. Keys at registry.ts:331,341,351,361,379,389,397,405,475,485,495,505,515,528,538,549,559,569,579,588,596,605,614,624,634,644,1979,2856. APP_URL (:371) is the only build-tier key with a live reader. lib/config/config-values.ts:9-11,225 explicitly and wrongly claim TOTAL_CHECKS_LABEL and SEO_OG_IMAGE are runtime-overridable.
findings.impact: An admin edits a setting, sees it save, and it never takes effect, including after a rebuild. Twenty-eight controls in the admin panel are decorative.
findings.recommendation: Either add a build-time reader that materialises these into the compiled config, reclassify them as runtime with real readers, or remove them from the registry. The false claim in config-values.ts:9-11,225 should be corrected regardless.

findings.title: BILLING_ENABLED is a runtime toggle whose hide-pricing half is read from a compiled constant in eleven places
findings.description: registry.ts:796-803 marks BILLING_ENABLED runtime tier with help reading 'Turning this off ... hides pricing.' The limit half is honoured live (lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts:120, lib/billing/plan-limits.ts:93/179/202). The hiding half is not: eleven surfaces read the compiled constant at lib/config/constants.ts:511 - app/pricing/page.tsx:68, app/pricing/layout.tsx:44, components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:22, components/landing/landing-cta.tsx:46, components/auth/auth-split-layout.tsx:33, components/profile/tabs/profile-billing-tab.tsx:186, components/modals/premium-upgrade-modal.tsx:164, all four app/checkout/**/page.tsx guards, and lib/billing/stripe.ts:37.
findings.impact: A self-hoster who turns billing off through the admin panel still has a live pricing page, a live nav link and live checkout routes until someone rebuilds. That is the exact scenario the runtime tier promises to handle.
findings.recommendation: Route the eleven consumers through the runtime setting rather than the compiled constant, or reclassify the key as build tier and correct its help text.

findings.title: Eight of nine feature flags are server-only or gate only half their surface, leaving dead UI and running workers
findings.description: Only FEATURE_PDF_REPORTS crosses to the browser (app/api/v3/config/client/route.ts:20,31 into use-client-config.ts into scan-actions-menu.tsx:545); a grep for each of the other eight in that route returns zero. Several also gate only half their surface, each verified individually: FEATURE_PDF_REPORTS hides the menu item but not the endpoint, since app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts has no getSetting reference and still serves ?format=pdf at :199-204; FEATURE_SCHEDULED_SCANS gates creation (schedules/route.ts:71) but not execution, since lib/scanner/scheduled-scans-worker.ts reads only its own concurrency settings, so existing schedules fire forever after the flag is off; FEATURE_WEBHOOKS gates registration (webhooks/route.ts:53) but not delivery, since lib/webhooks/*.ts contains no flag reference; FEATURE_TEAMS gates only POST (teams/route.ts:57) while GET, PATCH, DELETE, members/route.ts and app/teams/page.tsx are all ungated, contradicting the registry help at :665-672. By contrast POSTURE_DIGEST_ENABLED (posture-digest.ts:220) and DOMAIN_REVERIFY_ENABLED (reverify-worker.ts:60) do gate their workers correctly.
findings.impact: Disabling a feature leaves its UI fully present and its background work running. The user discovers the flag only via a 403 on submit, and scheduled scans and webhook deliveries continue to fire for a feature the operator believes is off.
findings.recommendation: Plumb the remaining eight flags through app/api/v3/config/client/route.ts so the UI can hide disabled features, and add the flag check to each feature's worker and endpoint, following the POSTURE_DIGEST_ENABLED pattern.

findings.title: Plan limits displayed to users come from a hardcoded catalog while enforcement reads 48 admin-editable settings
findings.description: components/pricing/pricing-features.tsx:186-187 carries the comment 'These numbers come straight out of the billing config, so this table cannot drift from what the API actually enforces', but it reads PLANS[].limits from lib/billing/catalog.ts:115-233, a hardcoded copy. Enforcement reads the 48 BILLING_* registry settings via lib/billing/plan-limits.ts:19-82. The same hardcoded read occurs at components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:157, components/modals/premium-upgrade-modal.tsx:79/89, app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:204,223,294, components/profile/tabs/profile-billing-tab.tsx:1493 and app/pricing/page.tsx:28-36. It is done correctly at app/api/v3/billing/route.ts:82-94 and app/api/v3/auth/me/route.ts:111,184, which resolve live.
findings.impact: Values match today so there is no present drift, but any one of 48 admin edits silently desynchronises what is advertised from what is enforced, on the pricing page, in the upgrade modal and on the checkout page. The comment asserting this cannot happen makes it less likely anyone checks.
findings.recommendation: Have the display surfaces resolve limits live the way app/api/v3/billing/route.ts:82-94 does, and delete the comment at pricing-features.tsx:186-187.

findings.title: Four notification categories exist in the backend with no account toggle, one with no control anywhere
findings.description: PUT /api/v3/account/notifications accepts any column in ALL_COLUMNS (lib/notifications/notifications.ts:17-44), which is 20 categories. components/profile/tabs/profile-notifications-tab.tsx renders 16. Missing: email_critical_findings (instrumentation.ts:811), email_posture_digest (lib/notifications/digest-schema.ts:41), email_product_updates (:825) and email_tips_guides (:826). Three are reachable only from the token-gated /unsubscribe page (app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:87,158,163). email_posture_digest has no control anywhere: the visible digest toggle at profile-notifications-tab.tsx:327 writes a different column, users.digest_email_enabled. Compounding, lib/notifications/posture-digest.ts:187 filters on digest_email_enabled and :239-242 sends via sendNotificationEmail({type: 'posture_digest'}), which re-checks the untoggleable email_posture_digest.
findings.impact: A user who unsubscribes from critical-finding emails can never re-enable them from their account. A user whose email_posture_digest was cleared by unsubscribe_all sees the profile digest toggle appear to work while nothing is ever sent. Marketing email is manageable only from an email footer link.
findings.recommendation: Add a row for email_critical_findings to the Scans card and a Product section mirroring app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:135-149. Resolve the two-gate posture digest by having the profile toggle write both columns or by collapsing them to one.

findings.title: Admin access rules cannot be edited, paused or given an expiry, and two render branches can never display
findings.description: app/api/v3/admin/features/route.ts:112,139,149 accept and insert expires_at, and :200-242 implements a full update action supporting value, description, reason, is_active and expires_at. Both columns are enforced at lib/scanner/access-rules.ts:62,103,113. components/admin/features/ip-rules-manager.tsx only ever dispatches create (:143) and delete (:185), and the create fetch at :141-151 omits expires_at. The rule drawer already renders 'Expires ...' at :435-443 and an Active/Inactive badge at :426-431, neither of which can ever show a non-default value. The list query also filters WHERE is_active = true (:169), so a rule deactivated via the API would vanish from the panel and could never be reactivated.
findings.impact: Every access rule an admin creates is permanent and uneditable. A temporary block on an abusive IP has to be created and later manually deleted, with no expiry and no pause, on a security surface where temporary is the normal case.
findings.recommendation: Add an expiry select (Never / 1h / 24h / 7d / 30d) to the Add Rule modal, an inline edit form, and an Active/Paused switch in the drawer. Change the list query to include inactive rules with a filter, so a paused rule remains reachable.

findings.title: The status poll uses a fixed 2000ms sleep with no early wake, adding up to 2 seconds of dead time after the scan completes
findings.description: The client polls GET /api/v3/scan/status/[id] on a fixed interval from lib/config/config-values.ts:555, with no backoff and no jitter, first poll immediate (app/dashboard/page.tsx:142, sleep at :160). Nothing wakes the loop when the server finishes.
findings.impact: Adds 0 to 2 seconds, averaging about 1, after the server is already done. Minor next to scan-01 but it becomes a third of the remaining wait once that is fixed.
findings.recommendation: Shorten the interval for the first ~10 seconds, or add SSE / long-poll to the status route.

findings.title: EPSS enrichment makes an uncached live FIRST.org call on the blocking path
findings.description: enrichFindingsWithExploitIntel is awaited at lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:720. lib/scanner/cve-enrichment.ts:214 explicitly does not cache EPSS scores across scans, unlike getKevCveIds which has both a memory and a DB cache at :190-210. The call has a 5 second ceiling.
findings.impact: Every scan whose findings name CVEs pays a live external round trip of up to 5 seconds, on the critical path, for data that changes daily at most.
findings.recommendation: Give fetchEpssScores the same memory-plus-DB cache getKevCveIds already has, or move enrichment after the status flip.

findings.title: runSyncChecks executes roughly 310 checks with no event-loop yields, stalling every other in-flight scan and poll
findings.description: lib/scanner/engine.ts:135-214, called from execute-scan.ts:616, runs the entire synchronous check set plus an HTML parse over up to 1MB in one uninterrupted block. In a single persistent Node process this blocks the event loop for every other request.
findings.impact: Estimated 100ms to 2s of blocking CPU per scan, during which every other user's scan I/O and every status poll is stalled. This is a cross-request amplifier, so its cost scales with concurrency rather than being per-scan.
findings.recommendation: Await a macrotask between check categories. Note this is the lowest-confidence item in the latency set: it is bounded from the code structure, not measured. Profile before investing.

findings.title: A blurred full-screen AI modal opens the instant results land, so a finished scan reads as still working
findings.description: app/dashboard/page.tsx:690-692 opens AiChoiceModal on completion, a fixed inset-0 backdrop-blur-xs overlay (components/scanner/ai-choice-modal.tsx:36). Results render underneath but the user must click Skip to see them.
findings.impact: Perceived latency on top of real latency. The scan finishes and the user is shown a blur, which is indistinguishable from more waiting.
findings.recommendation: Do not auto-open on completion. Offer the AI summary as an action on the results view instead, so the payoff of the scan is the first thing visible.

findings.title: The history view tabs wrap to two lines on mobile, breaking the underline baseline across four pages
findings.description: components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx:29 is `flex gap-1 border-b border-border/50` with links at `px-3 py-2` (:37). Four tabs need about 409px against 343px available. They do not overflow because min-width:auto floors them at about 294px; instead every multi-word label wraps ('Attack / Surface'), producing ragged tab heights and a broken border-b baseline. Affects /history, /assets, /attack-surface and /public-scans.
findings.impact: The primary navigation for four pages looks broken on every phone.
findings.recommendation: Add overflow-x-auto to line 29 and shrink-0 whitespace-nowrap to the Link at line 37.

findings.title: An invisible tag button sits under every history row's URL and steals the tap
findings.description: components/history/scan-tags.tsx:178-182 applies opacity-0 with group-hover and group-focus-within reveals. revealOnHover defaults to true and components/history/history-scan-row.tsx:134 uses the default. opacity-0 does not disable pointer events, and phones never hover, so a roughly 24x18px invisible button sits under every row's URL.
findings.impact: Tapping a scan row near the URL opens a tag input instead of the scan.
findings.recommendation: Add pointer-events-none with group-hover:pointer-events-auto and group-focus-within:pointer-events-auto, or use opacity-100 sm:opacity-0.

findings.title: The software inventory header clips its own count and chevron on mobile because the card is overflow-hidden
findings.description: components/scanner/software-inventory-panel.tsx:195-221. When vulnerableCount > 0 the header row measures about 363px against 343px at 375px and 358px at 390px. The card is overflow-hidden at :189, so the count and chevron are clipped rather than scrollable.
findings.impact: The component count and the expand affordance are invisible on a phone whenever the panel has something worth expanding for.
findings.recommendation: Line 198: add min-w-0 flex-1 truncate. Line 211: add hidden sm:inline.

findings.title: Dashboard analytics renders nothing on a failed fetch and throws on a partial payload
findings.description: components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:211-230 sets data only if d && d.severityBreakdown, catches by setting loading false, then returns null at :229. Only severityBreakdown is checked, but the render accesses data.sourceBreakdown.find (:242), data.dailyActivity.map (:244), data.topVulnerabilities.map (:255) and data.recentScans (:348) unguarded, so a partial response throws into app/dashboard/error.tsx.
findings.impact: A failing /api/v3/dashboard leaves the scan form followed by blank space with no message and no retry. A partial response takes out the whole route.
findings.recommendation: Render a distinct error state instead of null, and guard every field the render touches rather than only severityBreakdown.

findings.title: The activity tooltip prints '0 issues' for every day because the API hardcodes the field
findings.description: app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:102 returns issues: 0 for all 14 days; the SQL at :65-79 counts scans only. components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:325 renders `· ${d.issues} issues` whenever d.scans > 0.
findings.impact: Every activity bar tooltip reads 'N scans · 0 issues', which is visibly and confidently wrong on the main dashboard.
findings.recommendation: Either compute the real per-day issue count in the SQL or remove the clause from the tooltip. Do not ship a zero that looks like data.

findings.title: Any non-OK teams response logs a signed-in user out
findings.description: app/teams/page.tsx:109-113 is `if (!res.ok) { router.push("/login"); return; }` with no status check. Every sibling gates on 401 and 403 specifically (app/history/page.tsx:226, app/assets/page.tsx:74). The same shape exists at app/profile/page.tsx:296.
findings.impact: A transient 500, 503 or 429 bounces a still-authenticated user to the login screen, which reads as a session bug and erodes trust in the auth system.
findings.recommendation: Gate the redirect on 401 and 403 and render an error state otherwise, matching the sibling pages.

findings.title: The host page CTA says 'Scan example.com now' and scans vulnradar.dev instead
findings.description: app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:170-175 renders a button linking to ROUTES.DEMO with the label `Scan {data.host} now`. /demo has exactly one action, handleSelfScan, which hardcodes the target at app/demo/page.tsx:38 as `const siteUrl = window.location.origin;`. There is no target parameter.
findings.impact: The call to action on a public SEO landing page promises to scan the host the visitor came to see and scans the vendor's own site instead. This is the conversion path for organic traffic.
findings.recommendation: Link to `${ROUTES.DASHBOARD}?scan=${encodeURIComponent(data.host)}` - the dashboard already treats a dotted ?scan= value as a target (app/dashboard/page.tsx:70-72, 784-793) - or relabel the button to 'Try the scanner'.

findings.title: Five destructive or persisting actions fail silently across history, shares and teams
findings.description: components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:505-515 catches a failed Delete scan with only setDeleting(false), leaving the confirm dialog open and the spinner stopped with no explanation. app/shares/page.tsx:123-144 (revokeShare) and :100-121 (togglePubliclyListed) do nothing on a non-ok response, so the dialog closes or the toggle silently reverts. app/teams/page.tsx:428-457 (handleRename) is the only action on that page that does not set actionError. app/history/page.tsx:389-397 with components/history/history-notes.tsx:22-27 always exits edit mode, so on a failed PATCH the note stays on screen from local state while nothing was persisted; app/dashboard/page.tsx:375-387 catches and discards outright.
findings.impact: A user revokes a share and believes it is revoked. A user edits scan notes and believes they are saved. Neither happened. For share revocation specifically this is a security-relevant false confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Surface an error in every one of the five handlers, and for the notes case keep the editor open with the unsaved text rather than exiting on failure.

findings.title: The browser session viewer renders raw runtime error strings to the user
findings.description: app/browser/[id]/page.tsx:153-155 sets `e instanceof Error ? e.message : ...` and renders it at :546. A stale-deploy HTML response therefore surfaces `Unexpected token '<', "<!DOCTYPE "... is not valid JSON` to the user. The same shape at :319-323 renders {logsError} raw at :670-672, which can be literally 'HTTP 502'. For contrast components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:257-275 deliberately shows the scanner's message, and that is safe because app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:288-292 sets details to a fixed string.
findings.impact: Users see JSON parser internals. Given the known stale-deploy chunk-404 failure mode in this project, this is the error they are most likely to hit.
findings.recommendation: Keep the raw text in console.error and render a fixed sentence.

findings.title: activeTab is never reset between findings, so opening a finding with fewer code examples throws
findings.description: components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:662 is useState(0) while :922-923 reads issue.codeExamples[activeTab].code. The component explicitly supports issue changing while mounted (useEffect keyed on issue.id at :675), and the sibling RemediationControl was given key={issue.id} at :826 for exactly this reason; activeTab was missed.
findings.impact: Going from a finding with three code examples (tab 2 open) to one with a single example throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading code)' and takes out the view.
findings.recommendation: Add key={issue.id} at the IssueDetail call sites, or clamp the index against codeExamples.length.

findings.title: The public scans table uses fixed pixel columns that crush the hostname at tablet widths
findings.description: components/public-scans/public-scans-table.tsx:7 and components/public-scans/public-scan-row.tsx:22 use grid-cols-[1fr_150px_150px_90px] with gap-4, which is 390px of fixed columns plus 48px of gaps. At the sm breakpoint (640px) the Site column collapses to about 120px so nearly every hostname truncates, while 'Verdict' renders the word 'Clean' inside 150px.
findings.impact: The one column carrying the information is starved while two columns hold whitespace, on a public directory page.
findings.recommendation: Use sm:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_90px_150px_120px], or move the grid to the md breakpoint and keep the stacked layout through tablet.

findings.title: The pagination control overflows the viewport once a user passes 50 scans
findings.description: components/ui/pagination-control.tsx:118-208 is flex items-center gap-1 with no wrap: four arrow buttons at h-8 w-8 plus up to seven number or ellipsis slots at min-w-8 (:151-177), about 388px against 343px. Reached on /history and /assets at page size 10 once a user has more than 50 scans.
findings.impact: Horizontal page scroll appears on the two most-used list pages as soon as a user has real data.
findings.recommendation: Add flex-wrap justify-center at line 119, or hide the first and last page buttons below sm.

findings.title: Route error and loading boundaries exist for five routes and are missing on the other eight core routes plus all public content
findings.description: error.tsx exists for /dashboard, /history, /shares, /assets, /teams, /admin, /profile, /compare only. Missing on /repos, /badge, /public-scans, /attack-surface, /host/[hostname], /shared/[token], /browser/[id], /demo, /changelog, /checks, /alternatives, /tools, /docs, /legal, /contact, /pricing, /donate, /security and all of /checkout. loading.tsx has the same gaps, and /checkout has none despite components/billing/checkout-skeleton.tsx existing. app/dashboard/error.tsx:9-16 states the intent: it keeps the surrounding chrome intact. Additionally app/admin/error.tsx lacks the role="alert" and icon aria-hidden that app/profile/error.tsx:20,26 has.
findings.impact: A thrown error on any of those routes falls through to the root boundary, losing the page chrome and dropping the user onto a bare error screen. That covers roughly 790 public pages, since only /compare has its own boundary.
findings.recommendation: Add error.tsx to the eight missing core routes and to the public content sections, following app/dashboard/error.tsx. Add loading.tsx to /checkout wrapping the existing CheckoutSkeleton. Bring app/admin/error.tsx in line with app/profile/error.tsx.

findings.title: The root 404 has no public chrome and its primary button sends logged-out visitors to the dashboard
findings.description: No in-scope content route has its own not-found.tsx, so all three dynamic content routes fall through to the root one, which renders no LandingNav, no Footer, and a primary button linking to ROUTES.DASHBOARD. The same shape applies to app/error.tsx:103.
findings.impact: A logged-out visitor landing on a stale /checks/some-renamed-id from a search result gets a chrome-less 404 whose main button bounces them through middleware to /login. The likeliest visitor to a dead check URL is exactly the person with no account.
findings.recommendation: Add app/checks/not-found.tsx and app/alternatives/not-found.tsx wrapping SeoPageShell, or make the root 404's primary button conditional on auth and default it to ROUTES.LANDING.

findings.title: /public-scans shows three private tabs to anonymous visitors, all of which bounce to login
findings.description: app/public-scans/page.tsx:114 renders HistoryViewTabs unconditionally on a page anonymous visitors can reach. 'My History', 'Assets' and 'Attack Surface' all redirect a guest to /login.
findings.impact: Three of four tabs on a public page are traps for the exact audience the page exists to serve.
findings.recommendation: Gate the three private tabs behind useAuth() inside components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx:8-13.

findings.title: All ten admin sticky table headers are inert because a second scroll container sits between the header and the height cap
findings.description: components/admin/shared/data-table.tsx:130 applies maxHeight to an outer `overflow-auto` div, but components/ui/table.tsx:9 wraps the table in its own `relative w-full overflow-auto` div with no height cap. position: sticky binds to the nearest scrolling ancestor, which is the inner uncapped div whose scrollTop is permanently 0, so sticky top-0 on TableHeader never engages while the outer container does the actual scrolling.
findings.impact: Column headers scroll away on all ten admin tables. Worst on the eight-column Engine Feedback table, where the meaning of each column is lost after one scroll.
findings.recommendation: Move the maxHeight onto the components/ui/table.tsx wrapper, or have TableScrollArea render a bare <table> without the extra div.

findings.title: Five admin panels render confident wrong values when their fetch fails, including a settings page showing false defaults
findings.description: Each renders a plausible but incorrect state instead of an error: components/admin/features/backup-manager.tsx:81 shows 'Last backup: Never'; components/admin/features/updater-manager.tsx:116 shows 'cosign: Not installed'; components/admin/features/system-settings-manager.tsx:108 shows every setting at its shipped default with no Customized badges; components/admin/features/queue-status-manager.tsx:136 shows skeletons forever; components/admin/features/billing-overview-manager.tsx:238 shows header-only tables.
findings.impact: The system-settings case is the dangerous one: an admin edits from a false baseline and can silently revert real configuration across the whole product. The backup case tells an operator they have no backups when they may have many.
findings.recommendation: Check res.ok in each and render a distinct error state. Prioritise system-settings-manager, where the failure mode causes data loss rather than confusion.

findings.title: Every system-settings tab shares one id, and that id is the React key, so the mobile drawer jumps to the wrong tab
findings.description: components/admin/features/system-settings-manager.tsx:92 gives every tab entry id: "settings-panel", and that id is used as the React key at components/admin/shared/admin-mobile-toc.tsx:200.
findings.impact: Tapping one tab in the mobile drawer can switch to a different one.
findings.recommendation: Give each tab a unique id.

findings.title: The admin toast has no width cap, so server error strings clip off-screen on mobile
findings.description: components/admin/shared/toast.tsx:24 is fixed bottom-4 right-4 z-50 with no max-w constraint.
findings.impact: The error message an admin needs to read is the part that runs off the edge of the screen.
findings.recommendation: Add max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)] sm:max-w-sm.

findings.title: The impersonation banner overflows on mobile, causing horizontal scroll on every page while impersonating
findings.description: components/admin/impersonation-banner.tsx:85-88 is a centred flex row with no truncate, no min-w-0 and no flex-wrap anywhere in the file. At 375px the content measures roughly 380px against 343px available, before the optional error span at :101 adds about 150px more. With justify-center the overflow splits both sides. It is mounted in app/layout.tsx:181, so it affects every page.
findings.impact: Horizontal page scroll across the entire app while impersonating, with the 'Stop impersonating' button pushed partly off the right edge - the one control the admin most needs.
findings.recommendation: Add flex-wrap, min-w-0 on the span, truncate max-w-[45vw] on the email, and shrink-0 on the button.

findings.title: The audit-log filter strip hides seven of ten filters on mobile with no scrollbar
findings.description: components/admin/audit/audit-log.tsx:283 is `flex gap-2 overflow-x-auto pb-2 sm:pb-0 sm:flex-wrap scrollbar-hide`, the last remaining overflow-x-auto scrollbar-hide strip in admin. components/admin/features/email-logs-manager.tsx:284 wraps instead of scrolling.
findings.impact: Seven of ten audit filters are invisible on a phone, with scrollbar-hide removing the only cue that more exist.
findings.recommendation: Bring in line with components/admin/features/email-logs-manager.tsx:284 and wrap rather than scroll.

findings.title: Four sticky sidebars ignore the banner offset variables the nav uses, so the nav paints over them
findings.description: app/admin/page.tsx:1052 is `sticky top-20`, and components/docs/docs-sidebar.tsx:27 and components/docs/docs-toc.tsx:17 are `sticky top-16`. components/scanner/header.tsx:120 shifts by calc(var(--vr-banner-h,0px) + var(--vr-imp-banner-h,0px)) and components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:49 shifts by top-(--vr-banner-h,0px) at z-50. components/shared/site-notifications.tsx:586 sets --vr-banner-h live and components/admin/impersonation-banner.tsx:41-53 sets --vr-imp-banner-h. app/profile/page.tsx:746 is the correct pattern, though even it omits --vr-imp-banner-h. Since impersonation is an admin feature, app/admin/page.tsx:1052 is guaranteed to fail during impersonation.
findings.impact: With a banner showing, the nav slides down over the top rows of these sidebars and they stop being clickable. The docs pair additionally has a 7px dead band even with no banner, since top-16 is 64px against a 57px nav.
findings.recommendation: Use top-[calc(5rem+var(--vr-banner-h,0px)+var(--vr-imp-banner-h,0px))] transition-[top] duration-300 on all four, following app/profile/page.tsx:746.

findings.title: The admin mobile Contents pill is z-40 under z-50 save bars, locking admins out of tab switching mid-edit
findings.description: components/admin/shared/admin-mobile-toc.tsx:42 is z-40 while the save bars at components/admin/features/system-settings-manager.tsx:664 and components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:2731 are z-50. On System Settings the TabsList is hidden lg:flex, so that pill is the only mobile tab switcher.
findings.impact: Editing one field on a phone raises the save bar, which covers the pill, which locks the admin out of switching tabs until they save or discard.
findings.recommendation: Raise the pill to z-50 and offset it above the save bar when one is showing.

findings.title: Five different page shells across the public surface, with /pricing hand-rolled and /donate having none
findings.description: PublicPageShell (components/shared/public-page-shell.tsx:32) swaps `isLoggedIn ? <Header/> : <LandingNav/>` at :58, covering /changelog, /compare, /contact, /security, /host/[hostname], /public-scans, /shared/[token]. DocsShell, LegalShell and SeoPageShell all use LandingNav unconditionally. /pricing is hand-rolled and renders <LandingNav /> twice (app/pricing/page.tsx:71 and :150) despite computing isLoggedIn at :66. /donate has no nav, no <main> and no footer at all. LandingNav is itself auth-aware (components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:104), so the swap is redundant.
findings.impact: A signed-in user clicking Changelog, then Docs, then Changelog watches the header change identity twice. /donate is a page with no way off it.
findings.recommendation: Move /pricing and /donate onto PublicPageShell and pick one convention for the signed-in header across the four public shells. The non-negotiable half is shell-01: the skip-link id should live in one shell rather than being forgotten by three.

findings.title: The subscription is created before card validation, leaving an orphan incomplete subscription on every typo
findings.description: components/billing/stripe-checkout.tsx:210 creates the Stripe subscription before calling elements.submit(). The other three billing components validate first and carry a comment explaining why.
findings.impact: Every mistyped card leaves an orphan incomplete subscription on the customer record, polluting billing data and potentially triggering dunning.
findings.recommendation: Call elements.submit() first, matching components/billing/ai-credit-checkout.tsx.

findings.title: The checkout success page only understands subscriptions, so credit top-ups warn about a payment that succeeded
findings.description: app/checkout/success/checkout-success-content.tsx:13 is the return_url for all four checkout flows but only polls verify-subscription. A redirect-method credit top-up polls for about 22.5 seconds and then warns the payment could not be confirmed. redirect_status=failed is ignored entirely, so a genuinely failed payment also lands on a page implying success is pending.
findings.impact: A successful purchase is reported as possibly failed, and a failed purchase is reported as probably fine. Both directions are wrong on the money path.
findings.recommendation: Branch on the product type in the return URL and read redirect_status.

findings.title: The support tickets section renders nothing while loading, so /contact looks like the feature is missing
findings.description: components/contact/support-tickets.tsx:174 is `if (isLoading) return null`, under the first and most prominent category on /contact.
findings.impact: On a cold load the page appears not to have a ticket feature at all.
findings.recommendation: Render a skeleton instead of null.

findings.title: /donate removes its own fallback link at the moment it is needed and traps the back button in a redirect loop
findings.description: app/donate/page.tsx:14-22 redirects via window.location.href after 100ms and sets redirected true. At :51-60 the manual 'Continue to Stripe' button renders only when !redirected, and a thank-you message replaces it when redirected. Three defects compound: the fallback disappears exactly when the automatic redirect has failed; location.href rather than location.replace() leaves /donate in history, so Back from Stripe returns here and re-fires after 100ms; and the page has no nav, no <main> and no footer, so a stranded user has no way off it.
findings.impact: A user whose redirect fails is shown a thank-you for a donation that never happened, with no link to complete it and no navigation. Pressing Back from Stripe creates an inescapable loop.
findings.recommendation: Use location.replace(), keep the fallback link rendered unconditionally, drop the premature thank-you, and wrap the page in PublicPageShell.

findings.title: Checkout columns are misaligned between 768px and 1024px by a hardcoded top padding
findings.description: app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:306 uses a magic md:pt-[120px] to align the second column.
findings.impact: The two columns visibly misalign across the whole tablet band on the payment page.
findings.recommendation: Align with a grid row rather than a hardcoded pixel offset.

findings.title: The ToS gate blocks the unsubscribe link in every marketing email
findings.description: components/auth/tos-gate.tsx:9 sets SKIP_TOS_PATHS to ["/login", "/signup", "/legal"]. The logged-out path is fine because :28-31 sets status skip when /api/v3/auth/me is not ok. The exposure is a signed-in user with pending or needs_reaccept status, for whom the page renders at opacity-20 blur-xs pointer-events-none behind TosModal (:77-91). /unsubscribe, /verify-email and /reset-password are not in the skip list.
findings.impact: The unsubscribe link in every marketing email is gated behind accepting updated terms. Coupled with auth-05, the unsubscribe flow is compromised at both ends.
findings.recommendation: Add "/unsubscribe", "/verify-email", "/reset-password" and "/forgot-password" to SKIP_TOS_PATHS.
