findings.title: Auth pages prerender a null Suspense fallback, so first paint is empty and the indexable /login is one empty div
findings.description: app/reset-password/page.tsx:41 uses Suspense fallback={null}, prerendered into the static HTML, while the pitch column is hidden lg:block. First paint on a phone is wordmark, empty band, footer. The same shape at app/login/page.tsx:12 and app/signup/page.tsx:12 replaces the entire page.
findings.impact: A blank first paint on the three highest-intent pages in the product, and the HTML a crawler receives for the indexable /login is a single empty div.
findings.recommendation: Give each Suspense a real skeleton fallback.

findings.title: The unsubscribe page prints an email address with no break-all and scrolls the page sideways
findings.description: app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:293 and :324 render redactEmail() output with no break-all, while three sibling components have it.
findings.impact: A long address scrolls the whole page horizontally.
findings.recommendation: Add break-all.

findings.title: Unsubscribe toggles are 24px tall and the destructive action is a 16px target at 60% opacity
findings.description: The 19 Switch toggles are 24x44px with the row's py-3 outside the hit area. The destructive 'unsubscribe from all' at app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:378 is a roughly 16px target at text-xs and 60% opacity.
findings.impact: A compliance-relevant preference screen is hard to operate accurately on a phone, and the most consequential control on it is the hardest to hit.
findings.recommendation: Make the whole row the label and hit area; promote the destructive action to h-11.

findings.title: The unsubscribe page crushes 19 preference rows into max-w-sm while an unused wide variant exists for exactly this screen
findings.description: app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:393 renders a 19-row preference list inside max-w-sm, leaving about 1050px empty on either side at 1440px. components/auth/auth-layout.tsx:9-11 documents an unused width="wide" prop with a docstring saying it is 'for the one screen that is a list rather than a form', which is this screen.
findings.impact: The page is needlessly cramped, and the fix already exists in the codebase unused.
findings.recommendation: Pass width="wide".

findings.title: A transient 500 on /api/v3/auth/me logs an authenticated user out of their own profile
findings.description: app/profile/page.tsx:296 redirects to /login on any non-ok response with no 401 check.
findings.impact: A still-authenticated user is bounced to the login screen by a transient server error, which reads as a session bug.
findings.recommendation: Redirect only on 401 and render an error state otherwise.

findings.title: The docs mobile drawer declares modality it does not enforce and its close button scrolls out of reach
findings.description: components/docs/docs-mobile-nav.tsx:65-84 declares role="dialog" aria-modal="true" at :70-71 but has no focus trap, so Tab walks straight out into the fully focusable page behind. There is no body scroll lock, so the page behind scroll-chains at the drawer's ends. The close X is absolute right-3 top-3 at :81, positioned against the padding box of the fixed element that is itself the scroll container (overflow-y-auto at :73); the drawer holds 19 two-line nav links plus the full page TOC, easily 1200px against a 667px phone, so the X scrolls out of reach within one swipe. It does get Escape (:57-59) and initial focus (:55) right.
findings.impact: A screen-reader user is told the drawer is modal and then tabs into hidden content behind it. Any user who scrolls loses the close button.
findings.recommendation: Move the content into an inner overflow-y-auto div and keep the close button a direct child of the fixed element (or sticky top-3); add body scroll lock to the existing open effect with cleanup; add a Tab-cycling branch to the existing keydown handler.

findings.title: Docs prose runs about 124 characters per line at 1440px on eight of twenty pages
findings.description: At 1440px the docs article column is 880px. Ten pages cap prose at max-w-[68ch] (about 483px); eight cap only the first paragraph and let the rest run the full 880px, roughly double the readable measure. Drifted: cli, architecture, rate-limits, webhooks, setup, self-hosting, developers, extension. Correct: github, sharing, account-security, triage, scheduled-scans, ai, api, reports. Representative offender app/docs/cli/page.tsx:59 constrained versus :74, 86, 93, 108, 174, 183, 194 unconstrained.
findings.impact: Half the documentation is materially harder to read on a desktop, and the inconsistency between adjacent pages is visible.
findings.recommendation: Put max-w-[68ch] once on the DocsSection body wrapper at components/docs/docs-section.tsx:55 so no page can drift again. The class is already the house standard (components/docs/docs-callout.tsx:83).

findings.title: The docs shell is 144px wider per side than its own nav above 1440px
findings.description: components/docs/docs-shell.tsx:60 is max-w-360 (1440px) while components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:53 is max-w-6xl (1152px). Docs is the only section wider than the nav above it. At 1920px the logo sits at x about 384 while the docs sidebar's left edge sits at x about 240.
findings.impact: The logo visibly floats inward from the content beneath it on every docs page at large widths.
findings.recommendation: Cap the docs shell at max-w-[calc(72rem+30rem)], or give LandingNav a containerClass prop. Capping is the smaller change.

findings.title: /checks ships roughly 754 list items and 190KB of HTML that never paints
findings.description: app/checks/page.tsx:147-188 renders an <li> for every one of roughly 754 checks across 18 categories, each with a SeverityPill carrying three inline style properties and a Link, all inside collapsed <details> elements.
findings.impact: Slow first paint on a phone, on the page whose entire purpose is to rank in search and be read by mobile arrivals.
findings.recommendation: Inline only the first N categories and link the rest to the existing /checks/category/[category] pages, or move the full index behind a crawlable ?all=1. The 754 individual check pages are intentional SEO surface and stay.

findings.title: API playground form inputs have no associated labels, contradicting the published accessibility statement
findings.description: app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:511-518 renders a <label> with no htmlFor beside an <Input> with no id, repeated per expanded endpoint card. Same at :403-412 for the request-body textarea. The API-key field 300 lines earlier does it correctly with htmlFor="api-key" and id="api-key" at :202-211, so this is inconsistency rather than ignorance. app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:89-90 claims 'All form inputs have associated labels for clarity.'
findings.impact: An expanded POST /scan card stacks four or five unlabeled text boxes; a screen-reader user hears five identical unnamed inputs. It also makes a published legal claim false.
findings.recommendation: Thread useId() through ParamField: const id = useId(), then htmlFor={id} and id={id}. Same for the body textarea.

findings.title: publiclyListed on the share POST is silently ignored for an existing live share
findings.description: app/api/v3/history/[id]/share/route.ts:65-77 validates publiclyListed, but the early return at :109-122 for a live non-expired token skips share_publicly_listed entirely; it is only applied at :134-139 when creating a genuinely new share. Latent today because both UI toggles use the dedicated PUT .../share/publicly-listed.
findings.impact: Harmless now, but it will silently drop the value for whoever adds the expiry control from drift-02 to the same request.
findings.recommendation: Apply publiclyListed in the existing-share branch as well, or reject the field there explicitly rather than ignoring it.

findings.title: Twelve schema columns are written and never read, or defined and never written
findings.description: Verified dead, each with the grep that found no live reference: users.beta_access (:303) hardcoded false in every INSERT (lib/auth/auth.ts:282,361,382; staff-invite/[token]/route.ts:199), no UPDATE, no gate; users.email_session_revoked (:317) a legacy duplicate whose nine live references all resolve to notification_preferences; users.daily_scan_limit (:304) see drift-05; broadcast_recipients.opened_at and .clicked_at (:1155-1156) DDL only; broadcast_messages.scheduled_at (:1137) inserted but no worker consumes it and status is hardcoded 'draft' then 'sent', so the CHECK values 'scheduled' and 'cancelled' are unwritable; broadcast_messages.message_type (:1135) hardcoded "email" by the UI and never read by the send path (:504); data_requests.completed_at (:876) DDL only, the route uses downloaded_at; system_settings.setting_type (:1121) DDL only; gifted_subscriptions.reason (:950) selected in the GDPR export but the only INSERT (admin/route.ts:1671) omits it and the gift dialog has no field; badges.is_limited (:496) only ever inserted as false with no UPDATE anywhere; api_keys.team_id (:931) no reference in lib/api/api-keys.ts or app/api/v3/keys; scan_screenshots.width and .height (:1381-1382) written at lib/scanner/page-screenshot.ts:295, never selected, consumers read the result_meta copy.
findings.impact: Schema noise that misleads anyone reading the model, plus three cases (beta_access, message_type, scheduled_at) that look like shipped features and are not.
findings.recommendation: Decide per column: wire it or drop it. Deletions need owner sign-off. beta_access, broadcast scheduling and broadcast message_type are the three worth a product decision rather than a silent drop.

findings.title: Fifteen permission constants gate nothing, including two for a reports feature that does not exist
findings.description: Dead constants in lib/auth/permissions-client.ts: VIEW_USER_API_KEYS (:29), DELETE_ANY_TEAM (:76), VIEW_REPORTS (:80) and RESOLVE_REPORTS (:81) - there is no reports feature or table at all - VIEW_DEBUG_INFO (:92), CLEAR_CACHE (:94), SEND_USER_EMAILS (:85), ACCESS_ADMIN_PANEL (:11), ACCESS_STAFF_PAGE (:12) granted to six roles while app/staff does not exist, VIEW_USER_SESSIONS (:27), VIEW_BADGES (:34), VIEW_ALL_SCANS (:41), VIEW_SCAN_STATS (:43), VIEW_SUBSCRIPTIONS (:47), MANAGE_SUBSCRIPTIONS (:48). requireModerator() at lib/auth/authorization.ts:102-122 has zero call sites. Separately, several cards render ungated where a permission exists for them: the API Keys card at user-detail-panel.tsx:2561, sessions at :2667, all-scans at :2507, and badges at admin/route.ts:281-286 which has no permission call unlike its neighbours at :249 and :294.
findings.impact: An operator granting or withholding these permissions changes nothing, which is a security-adjacent false assurance. The ungated cards are the mirror image: data visible to staff roles that were never granted access to it.
findings.recommendation: Split into two passes: wire the four ungated cards to their existing permissions first, since that is a real access-control gap; then delete or implement the fifteen dead constants.

findings.title: Eight admin permission and UI gate mismatches, including one that exposes every AI conversation to any staff role
findings.description: The ai-chats tab requires MODERATE_CONTENT at app/admin/page.tsx:756 while its API only calls requireStaff() (app/api/v3/ai/conversations/route.ts:99), so any staff role can read every AI conversation by calling the endpoint directly. The 'Active Staff' tab at :705 has no gate but its API requires VIEW_AUDIT_LOG (admin/route.ts:294), guaranteeing a 403 for billing, content_manager and ops. EDIT_USER_EMAIL and EDIT_USER_PLAN gate nothing because the editors use canManageStaff (user-detail-panel.tsx:878,894,968,1019). The Staff Role card is gated on DELETE_USER (:1106) rather than EDIT_USER_ROLE. send_email has a permission (:85), a role grant (:178) and a success toast (app/admin/page.tsx:557) but no backend case, so it would 400; the repo's own test flags this at tests/lib/auth/permissions-client.test.ts:323-327.
findings.impact: One genuine authorization gap (AI conversations readable by any staff role via the API), one guaranteed-broken tab, and several controls whose permission labels do not describe what they actually check.
findings.recommendation: Fix the ai-chats API gate first: add the MODERATE_CONTENT check to app/api/v3/ai/conversations/route.ts so it matches its tab. Then align the remaining gates with the permissions their labels claim, and either implement or remove send_email.

findings.title: Seven runtime-tier settings have no reader or are read via the compiled constant
findings.description: The runtime tier promises effect within the 30 second TTL, so there is no 'next build' excuse. Dead: ENTERPRISE_EMAIL (registry.ts:456, never rendered), BILLING_HISTORY_PAGE_SIZE (:904, zero readers and no invoice route exists to consume it), SITE_NOTIFICATION_DEFAULT_DISMISS_DAYS (:2595, zero readers while components/shared/site-notifications.tsx:58-59 hardcodes 30 days - exactly the drift the constant was meant to prevent), MAX_EMAIL_LENGTH (:2655, reached only through the dead DATABASE object at lib/config/constants.ts:478-484). Read from the constant instead of the setting: POSTURE_DIGEST_MAX_FINDINGS_LISTED (:775 vs lib/notifications/posture-digest.ts:46,155), DOMAIN_REVERIFY_TICK_INTERVAL_MS (:737 vs lib/scanner/reverify-worker.ts:28,117,125), PAGINATION_MAX_PAGE_SIZE (:2763 vs four routes importing the constant). Also CONFIG_BACKGROUND_COLOR_LIGHT (config-values.ts:190, registry.ts:505) is admin-editable with no corresponding export, so it changes nothing.
findings.impact: Eight more admin controls that appear to work and do not, on top of the 28 build-tier ones in drift-07.
findings.recommendation: Wire the readers or remove the keys. SITE_NOTIFICATION_DEFAULT_DISMISS_DAYS is the clearest single fix: point site-notifications.tsx:58-59 at the setting.

findings.title: Nineteen API capabilities exist with no UI control, each with a specific screen it belongs on
findings.description: Verified by reading each handler. POST /api/v3/scan/import-spec (parses OpenAPI 3, Swagger 2 and Postman, returns targets) has no UI caller; API.SCAN_IMPORT_SPEC exists at lib/config/client-constants.ts:145 referenced only by the changelog - belongs on the bulk tab of components/scanner/scan-form.tsx. Authenticated crawl is unreachable: app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:216,300-337 accepts the same auth block, but app/dashboard/page.tsx:415-449 routes any request carrying auth to the single-page endpoint, so deep plus a login silently downgrades. PATCH /api/v3/teams/members (role change, with ceiling and self-demotion guards) has no caller; the only way to change a teammate's role is remove and re-invite - belongs on components/teams/team-members-list.tsx:160. PATCH /api/v3/account/discord (syncAvatar, syncName) unreachable while components/modals/discord-profile-modal.tsx:27-28 has exactly those checkboxes but POSTs OAuth query-string values to /api/v3/auth/update, so it only works in the seconds after connecting. Badge revoke (DELETE /api/v3/badge/site?scanId=N, sets revoked_at) has no caller, so a badge pasted into a public README cannot be killed - belongs under the ScopeToggle at components/badge/badge-preview.tsx:261. Support tickets cannot be reopened: the route permits it at app/api/v3/support-tickets/[id]/route.ts:321-328 but both UIs only send resolved and closed, and replying to a closed ticket 409s. The updater can only install the newest release (app/api/v3/admin/updater/apply/route.ts:94,120-123 accepts any targetVersion; components/admin/features/updater-manager.tsx:185 always sends status.latest) so there is no rollback or pin. /api/v3/health returns schema_version vs schema_required, missing_tables, latency and pool stats and has no consumer, so a self-hoster needing a migration has no in-app signal. Stripe setup is curl-only, and both routes gate on role !== ADMIN exactly (setup-products/route.ts:31, setup-webhook/route.ts:36) which locks out super_admin unlike every other admin route. Also: teamId on schedules and webhooks, webhook type pinning (both UI paths hardcode "auto"), GitHub repo scan branch/ref, per-finding feedback notes, browser session viewport and ttlSeconds (the latter hardcoded to 360 at scan-actions-menu.tsx:384, defeating the admin setting), security alerts limit/offset/severity/user_id (hardcoded to 100 so alert 101 is unreachable), admin AI-conversations userId filter, admin notification email tone (hardcoded "info"), history rescan dropping all original scan options, scan source 'scheduled' rendering as "Web", admin content and public directory page sizes, and markAllRead on the notification bell.
findings.impact: Nineteen shipped backend capabilities that no user can reach. Several are not conveniences: badge revoke has no alternative, authenticated crawl silently does something other than what was asked, and the health endpoint is the only signal a self-hoster has that their schema is behind.
findings.recommendation: Triage by user harm rather than effort. Highest first: authenticated crawl (silent wrong behaviour), badge revoke (no alternative exists), team member role change (workaround is destructive), support ticket reopen (dead end), health panel (self-host blocker). The rest are ordinary missing controls.

findings.title: Four backend capabilities are gated behind conditions nothing can satisfy
findings.description: domains.team_id (instrumentation.ts:3176) is read for team access at app/api/v3/domains/route.ts:33, but the INSERT at :120 omits it, no PATCH exists anywhere under app/api/v3/domains/ (exports are GET, POST, DELETE plus verify POST), all four UPDATE/INSERT statements skip it, and components/profile/tabs/domains-section.tsx:147 hardcodes team_id: null - yet app/docs/teams/page.tsx:425 documents it as a feature. DEFAULT_API_KEY_DAILY_LIMIT (registry.ts:1527-1536) is admin-editable and read at lib/api/api-keys.ts:70 via `dailyLimit ?? await getSetting(...)`, but generateApiKey has exactly one production caller (app/api/v3/keys/route.ts:95) which always passes an explicit number, so the branch is dead; compounding, app/docs/api/page.tsx:738 and app/docs/rate-limits/page.tsx:173 tell users the default is 50 while the real value is the plan's apiRequestsPerDay, 25 on Free. access_rules.is_active = false is writable via the API but the list query filters WHERE is_active = true (admin/features/route.ts:168), so a deactivated rule vanishes and can never be reactivated. The empty-string state of CHROME_WEB_STORE_URL and FIREFOX_ADDON_URL (registry.ts:397-412) is documented as falling back to a packaged release, but the admin write goes through z.url() which rejects "", the env path skips empty overrides (runtime-config.ts:89), and reset restores a non-empty default - and the fallback UI does not exist either, since app/docs/extension/page.tsx:113,139 link unconditionally under a hardcoded 'Live' badge.
findings.impact: Four documented behaviours that cannot occur. The API key limit case additionally publishes a wrong number to users in two docs pages.
findings.recommendation: Correct the two docs pages about the API key default immediately, since that is user-facing misinformation. Then either implement domains.team_id (a PATCH route plus a selector) or remove it and its docs claim.

findings.title: Two entitlements are enforced but never advertised, and one has no admin setting at all
findings.description: The crawl page-selection limit is hardcoded at lib/billing/crawl-page-limits.ts:18-23 (25/50/100/250) and enforced at app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:258, but a grep for CRAWL_PAGES in lib/config/registry.ts returns zero. It is the only per-plan entitlement with no registry key, so it is absent from Admin > Settings > Billing and from components/pricing/pricing-features.tsx, surfacing only at point of use (components/scanner/crawl-url-selector.tsx:50). githubReviewTokensPerWindow is enforced per plan but no plan's features array mentions GitHub review (only AI review tokens at lib/billing/catalog.ts:141,174,205), so a Free user hits a hard 403 with no prior signal. Separately, lib/billing/github-review-usage.ts:365-372 implements a free-plan trial whose own comment reads 'Hidden trial, never advertised on the pricing page', while Free's githubReviewTokensPerWindow of 0 makes components/pricing/pricing-features.tsx:85-89 render a cross for Free.
findings.impact: Two invisible paywalls that users meet as a 403 rather than as a plan comparison, and a genuine free-tier benefit that the pricing page actively denies exists.
findings.recommendation: Add BILLING_*_CRAWL_PAGES registry keys and a Scanning row on /pricing. Add a GitHub review row to the plan comparison. Decide whether the hidden trial should be advertised; if it stays hidden, stop rendering a cross for a capability Free actually has.

findings.title: The bulk remediation endpoint fans out 200 unbatched queries with no transaction, making its error message dishonest
findings.description: app/api/v3/scan/remediation/bulk/route.ts:83-119 issues Promise.all over up to 200 independent pool.query calls with no transaction. Partial failure leaves partial state while the UI shows a generic 'Couldn't apply. Try again.' Separately lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:366 declares security: [{ apiKey: [] }] for this route (and :337 for the single route) but neither handler has a Bearer path, so an API-key client following the published spec gets a 401.
findings.impact: A user who retries after a partial failure re-applies to findings already changed, and cannot tell which ones took. The endpoint has zero external consumers because the published spec is wrong about its auth.
findings.recommendation: Replace the fan-out with one INSERT ... SELECT ... FROM unnest(...) inside a transaction, then the all-or-nothing error copy becomes true. Correct or remove the apiKey security declaration in the OpenAPI spec. Note this is a prerequisite for the undo described in bulk-01.

findings.title: The opt-in screenshot wait is capped at 30 seconds, longer than the entire rest of the scan
findings.description: lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:812 awaits the screenshot with CONFIG_SCAN_SCREENSHOT_MAX_WAIT_MS = 30_000 (lib/config/config-values.ts:1013).
findings.impact: Only affects users who tick the box, but when it bites it more than doubles the wait.
findings.recommendation: Reduce the cap, or render results first and let the screenshot populate asynchronously.

findings.title: Admin badge multi-select conveys selection only visually and commits without a transaction
findings.description: components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:1162 (literally commented 'Badges - multi select'), state at :160-161, revoke chips at :1177-1233, award dialog at :1270-1360, commit at :434-453. The shape is right: selections queue as a staged diff, surface in the save-confirmation modal as +3 badges / -2 badges, and can be unqueued before commit. Three defects: the toggles are plain buttons with no aria-pressed, so selected state is conveyed only by ring-2, line-through and a title attribute; the commit is Promise.all of N separate PATCHes with no transaction; and each fires its own toast (app/admin/page.tsx:568) while racing on the single shared actionLoading string (:516, :586).
findings.impact: Low traffic, but a screen-reader user cannot tell which badges are staged, and a partial failure leaves partial awards with a burst of contradictory toasts.
findings.recommendation: Keep it. Add aria-pressed to both toggle sets, replace the N toasts with one summary toast, and either sequence the commit or accept the partial-failure risk explicitly. Roughly 30 lines. If removal is preferred instead, UserDetailPanel has exactly one importer (app/admin/page.tsx:147) and award_badge/revoke_badge survive independently.

findings.title: The crawl page picker is the best-built selection UI in the product and should be kept as is
findings.description: components/scanner/crawl-url-selector.tsx (283 lines), rendered from app/dashboard/page.tsx:963-970. Persistent footer toolbar with 'N of M selected (max L)', a search filter, and Select all / Clear all. Pre-selects up to the plan cap at :55-64; over-cap rows are disabled at 40% opacity with an explanatory banner. useModalA11y provides focus trap, Escape and focus restore. Mobile works at 320px via max-h-[80vh] with a min-h-0 flex-1 scroll list and text-base sm:text-xs to stop iOS zoom. The backend is a real bulk endpoint: one request carries the whole array and app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:235-272 re-validates and re-enforces the plan cap server-side.
findings.impact: None. Recorded so it is not swept up in a bulk-action removal pass: deleting it does not remove clutter, it removes the crawl feature or forces every crawl to scan every discovered page at the user's expense.
findings.recommendation: Keep. Two optional nits: the rows are buttons with aria-pressed and a fake check glyph rather than real checkboxes, so assistive tech does not announce them as checkboxes; and defaulting to everything pre-selected means a user who wants three pages must deselect the rest.

findings.title: Empty leftover directory at app/api/v3/admin/bulk/
findings.description: Empty directory left over from commit 52656312 ('remove bulk user actions'). Git does not track empty directories, so it survives only in the working tree. Useful precedent found alongside it: lib/changelog/data.ts:1063 records 'Removed Bulk User Actions' - the admin Users tab previously had exactly this kind of select-up-to-200 feature and it was deleted outright on blast-radius grounds.
findings.impact: None functional. Noted because the precedent is directly relevant to the bulk-01 decision.
findings.recommendation: rmdir.

findings.title: isNavItemActive has two identical ternary branches, so NavItem.exact does nothing
findings.description: components/docs/docs-nav.ts:152-154 is `return item.exact ? pathname === item.href : pathname === item.href;`. NavItem.exact is declared at components/docs/docs-types.ts:12 and set on /docs at docs-nav.ts:21. Used by docs-sidebar.tsx:48 and docs-mobile-nav.tsx:94.
findings.impact: Correct today only because every nav href is a distinct page. A future prefix-matched entry will silently fail to highlight.
findings.recommendation: Either implement the non-exact branch as `pathname === item.href || pathname.startsWith(`${item.href}/`)`, or delete the helper and inline the equality.

findings.title: Seven touch targets under 44px in the docs and legal navigation, worst at 20px
findings.description: components/legal/legal-toc.tsx:26-28 has no vertical padding at all, giving about 20px, and it is the primary navigation for 15-clause legal documents. Others: app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:433 about 26px; components/docs/docs-code-block.tsx:53-60 about 27px; components/legal/legal-nav.tsx:45 about 30px; components/docs/docs-toc.tsx:73-78 about 32px and this is the mobile TOC (xl:hidden); components/docs/docs-code-tabs.tsx:39 about 36px; components/docs/docs-mobile-nav.tsx:81 about 36px.
findings.impact: Legal and docs navigation is hard to operate accurately on a phone.
findings.recommendation: legal-toc.tsx:28 add py-2 -my-0.5 min-h-11 flex items-center; docs-toc.tsx:74 py-2.5; docs-code-block.tsx:54 px-2.5 py-2; docs-code-tabs.tsx:39 py-2.5; docs-mobile-nav.tsx:81 p-2.5 min-h-11 min-w-11.

findings.title: The only non-responsive multi-column grid in the content surface is on the docs setup page
findings.description: app/docs/setup/page.tsx:78 is `grid grid-cols-3 gap-2 sm:gap-4` with no responsive prefix. At 375px each tile gets about 109px with about 89px of content, so 'systemd / PM2' and '5 min deploy' wrap to two lines and the tiles end up uneven. It does not overflow, and the sm: override shows it was hand-tuned.
findings.impact: Minor visual inconsistency on the setup page, which is a high-intent page for self-hosters.
findings.recommendation: grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-3 gap-2 sm:gap-4.

findings.title: The changelog has no pagination fallback, so without IntersectionObserver it is a permanent loading state
findings.description: components/changelog/changelog-list.tsx:156-169 renders a sentinel div reading 'Loading more releases...' whenever hasMore. IntersectionObserver (:59) is the only path past the first four releases. Separately, if CHANGELOG were empty, visibleCount is 0 and hasMore false, so the page renders a header followed only by 'The beginning of VulnRadar'.
findings.impact: Without IntersectionObserver the page shows four releases and a spinner-shaped dead end.
findings.recommendation: Render a real <button onClick={() => setVisibleCount(c => c + LOAD_MORE_BATCH)}>Load more</button> alongside the sentinel, and add an explicit empty branch.

findings.title: Two tablist implementations declare tab roles with no tabpanel, aria-controls or arrow-key navigation
findings.description: components/docs/docs-code-tabs.tsx:30-49 and app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:420-443 render role="tablist" with role="tab" buttons, but the controlled CodeBlock at :51 is not role="tabpanel" and nothing carries aria-controls or aria-labelledby. Arrow-key roving focus, which the tab role implies, is absent.
findings.impact: Assistive tech announces a tab widget and then behaves like plain buttons, which is worse than plain buttons.
findings.recommendation: Either complete the pattern (panel gets role="tabpanel", id and aria-labelledby; buttons get id and aria-controls; add arrow keys) or drop the ARIA roles. For two or three code samples, dropping the roles is the better trade.

findings.title: Dead configuration objects and constants, including a FEATURES object where seven of eight members are unread
findings.description: The FEATURES object at lib/config/constants.ts:778-786 has exactly one live member: a grep for FEATURES.[A-Z_]+ outside lib/config returns one hit, lib/hooks/use-client-config.ts:33 reading .PDF_REPORTS. The other seven (DEMO_MODE, TEAMS, API_KEYS, WEBHOOKS, SCHEDULED_SCANS, BULK_SCANS, EMAIL_NOTIFICATIONS) are read nowhere; the underlying CONFIG_FEATURE_* values are alive via the registry, so only this convenience object is dead. Also dead: the DATABASE object (:478-484, no matches for DATABASE.[A-Z_]), PATTERNS (:338), PAGINATION (:500), ENTERPRISE_EMAIL (:641), AUTH_SESSION_MAX_AGE (:242), API_KEY_SCOPE_DESCRIPTIONS (client-constants.ts:346), CONFIG_API_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS (config-values.ts:660), CONFIG_FOOTER_TEXT (:191), HISTORY_REPORT (client-constants.ts:151, zero web callers - the export menu regenerates all five formats client-side, and only the extension uses the route). Catalog helpers getFreePlan (catalog.ts:305), isPaidPlan (:309) and getApiLimitForPlan (:318) have tests as their only callers. Five unused skeleton exports at components/admin/shared/skeleton.tsx:18,40,62,90,114 (about 110 lines). components/auth/auth-layout.tsx:9-11 documents a width="wide" prop no caller uses - see auth-11, which is the screen it was written for. lib/config/public-paths.ts:66 lists ROUTES.GDPR_REQUEST as "/legal/privacy#gdpr" but middleware.ts:265 matches on pathname, which never contains a fragment, so the entry can never match (harmless, line 49 covers it).
findings.impact: Cleanup only, but the HISTORY_REPORT case has a real consequence: the server route additionally runs attachRemediation (app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts:149-155), so extension-exported reports and web-exported reports are not byte-identical.
findings.recommendation: Deletions need owner sign-off. The one to act on regardless is the report divergence: decide whether the extension and the web app should produce the same file, and make them agree.

findings.title: Two archival and delivery tables are written on every event and read by nothing
findings.description: webhook_deliveries (instrumentation.ts:2328) is written on every attempt at lib/webhooks/delivery.ts:111 and never SELECTed; its index on (webhook_id, attempted_at DESC) is shaped for a UI that was never built. Already recorded as AUDIT-009 #185 and still open. admin_audit_log_archive (lib/database/audit-log-archive.ts:47) is created and INSERTed at :89, and a repo-wide grep returns only that file.
findings.impact: A user whose webhook is failing has no way to see why, despite the data being captured. Purged compliance history is unviewable by any screen, route or export, which undermines the point of archiving it.
findings.recommendation: Add a delivery log to Profile > Developer > Webhooks and an 'Archived batches' view to Admin > System > Audit Log. Both are read-only views over data that already exists.

findings.title: Webhook signing secrets cannot be rotated, unlike API keys
findings.description: webhooks.secret (instrumentation.ts:2313) is returned once at creation (app/api/v3/webhooks/route.ts:123) and the only UPDATE (app/api/v3/webhooks/[id]/route.ts:215) cannot set it. API keys have both rotate and revoke routes.
findings.impact: A leaked webhook secret can only be addressed by deleting the webhook and recreating it, which breaks the consumer's configuration.
findings.recommendation: Add a rotate path and a 'Rotate signing secret' control, mirroring the API key flow.

findings.title: API keys silently 403 from a new network because bound_ip is never shown and cannot be reset
findings.description: api_keys.bound_ip (instrumentation.ts:382) is enforced under API_KEY_IP_BINDING_ENABLED and auto-pins on first use (lib/api/api-keys.ts:213-266, :234). getUserApiKeys at :615-626 does not select it, no component references it, and there is no reset path.
findings.impact: When the feature is enabled, a key that worked yesterday starts returning 403 from a new network with no visible cause and no way to fix it short of issuing a new key.
findings.recommendation: Show the bound IP on the API keys list and add a 'Reset binding' action.

findings.title: Two parsed environment variables are never consulted, one of them documented
findings.description: CONTACT_EMAIL is parsed at lib/config/env.ts:85 and appears in .env.example and the docs, but the contact route sends to NOREPLY_EMAIL (app/api/v3/contact/route.ts:146). STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is parsed at :60 while only the NEXT_PUBLIC_ variant is ever read.
findings.impact: A self-hoster sets CONTACT_EMAIL as documented and contact mail goes elsewhere.
findings.recommendation: Either honour CONTACT_EMAIL in the contact route or remove it from env.ts, .env.example and the docs. Remove the unused STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY parse.

findings.title: Five admin actions have a backend case and no UI dispatch, and one has a toast with no backend case
findings.description: update_password (app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:732-754, sets a password and wipes sessions), revoke_all_sessions (:756-766, duplicating revoke_sessions at :824 which additionally emails), set_scan_limit (:1523, see drift-05), make_admin (:702) and remove_admin (:717, both superseded by set_role) all exist with no dispatch; they appear in components/admin/config.ts only as audit-log labels, and revoke_all_sessions is acknowledged as a naming bug at config.ts:303-306. export_data (:1272-1311, returns user, scans, apiKeys and badges) is likewise undispatched. Conversely app/admin/page.tsx:557 maps a send_email success toast for an action the PATCH switch has no case for, so it would 400. enable_user (:934) and delete_user/delete_account (:1985-1986) are unused aliases. Note the route's own comment at :779-786 argues against admin-set passwords, so update_password likely wants deleting rather than exposing.
findings.impact: Dead server-side surface plus one UI path that can only fail. export_data is the one with genuine user value, since GDPR export currently has no admin-side equivalent.
findings.recommendation: Wire export_data with a downloadBlob mirroring components/admin/audit/audit-log.tsx:90-107. Delete the rest, including the send_email toast.

findings.title: Seven client-sent fields are ignored by their handlers, one of them silently discarding user-chosen support categories
findings.description: app/api/v3/contact/route.ts:15-21 defines CATEGORY_LABELS for bug, feature, security, help and staff_application, then :109 does CATEGORY_LABELS[category] || "Other". The form offers nine (components/contact/contact-types.ts:27-82); billing (:58), enterprise (:64) and feedback (:76) are POSTed verbatim and land in the support inbox labelled 'Other'. Others: source: "bulk" sent at app/dashboard/page.tsx:753 while app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:374 computes source itself, so bulk scans are recorded as ordinary Web scans; authenticated and staff query params sent by components/shared/notification-center.tsx:293-296 and components/shared/site-notifications.tsx:683-686 to a route that derives both from the session and never reads searchParams, with the comment at site-notifications.tsx:678-682 now actively wrong in claiming they are enforced server-side; message_type hardcoded by mass-email-manager.tsx:132 and never read; userId in the 2FA verify body (components/auth/login-2fa-form.tsx:70,72) deliberately not destructured; baseUrl in the AI-config save (profile-ai-settings-tab.tsx:115,139) used only as an equality check, so sending it can only ever produce a 400.
findings.impact: The contact one is the only one with real user cost: triage information the user explicitly selected is discarded, and three categories are indistinguishable from 'Other' in the support inbox.
findings.recommendation: Add billing, enterprise and feedback to CATEGORY_LABELS - a one-line fix. Delete the dead params and the incorrect comment at site-notifications.tsx:678-682.

findings.title: The browser sessions API documents a TTL default 60 seconds below the real value and omits two accepted fields
findings.description: app/docs/api/page.tsx:525 and :539 advertise ttlSeconds and expiresInSeconds of 300, and :541 states ttlSeconds is hard-clamped to BROWSERBASE_MAX_TTL_SECONDS 'default 300 = 5 minutes'. The real value is 360 (lib/config/config-values.ts:913-914) and the route's floor is 30s (app/api/v3/browser/sessions/route.ts:52). The docs never mention the viewport body field (:34) nor the legacy ttl alias (:49).
findings.impact: viewport is unreachable from both surfaces: no UI control (see drift-21) and undocumented for API callers, who are currently its only possible consumers.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md states the brand is cyan/teal at ~190 degrees; every shipped surface is blue #60a5fa at 213 degrees
findings.description: app/globals.css:178, lib/config/config-values.ts:188 (CONFIG_PRIMARY_COLOR = "#60a5fa"), lib/config/brand.ts:16-21, public/og-image.svg:36,58 and the five store PNGs all agree on blue #60a5fa (213 94% 68%). The only 190 degree hue left in the system is --chart-1 (app/globals.css:197), which is unused. app/global-error.tsx:10 still hardcodes BRAND_TEAL = "#0891b2", a stale cyan matching nothing.
findings.impact: Every future contributor and every AI agent reading CLAUDE.md is told the wrong brand colour on line 1, which is how stale cyan keeps reappearing.
findings.recommendation: Correct CLAUDE.md line 1 to blue #60a5fa (213 degrees) and fix the BRAND_TEAL constant in app/global-error.tsx:10. See audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md for the full extracted spec.

findings.title: Inter and JetBrains Mono are imported and never applied; the site ships in system-ui
findings.description: app/layout.tsx:39-43 imports Inter and JetBrains_Mono from next/font/google but assigns both to underscore-prefixed unused consts, and their --font-inter and --font-jetbrains-mono variables are never applied. app/layout.tsx:170 is <body className="font-sans antialiased"> and tailwind.config.mjs has no fontFamily extension, so the real stack is Tailwind v4's ui-sans-serif / ui-monospace defaults.
findings.impact: Either two font downloads are being paid for and discarded, or the intended typography was never shipped. Both are worth knowing before any design work.
findings.recommendation: Decide which was intended: wire the CSS variables into tailwind.config.mjs, or remove the imports. Note the system stack is what every existing surface was visually tuned against, so switching to Inter is a visual change, not a no-op.

findings.title: components/ui/badge.tsx is the one primitive that hardcodes Tailwind palette colours and ignores dark mode
findings.description: components/ui/badge.tsx:16-19 defines info as bg-blue-500/10 text-blue-600, success as bg-green-500/10 text-green-600, warning as bg-amber-500/10 text-amber-600 and error as bg-red-500/10 text-red-600. These bypass the token set and do not respond to dark mode. The codebase is otherwise clean: zero bg-gray-*, text-gray-*, bg-slate-*, bg-zinc-* or border-gray-* anywhere in app/ or components/. Related: app/globals.css:9 safelists literal palette colours for role badges, :487-575 hardcodes hover and selection surfaces as literal hsl() with !important, --surface-1/2/3 are defined at :210-213 and used nowhere, and --sidebar-* is wired into tailwind.config.mjs:64-73 but never defined in CSS so those utilities resolve to nothing. Separately components/badge/badge-preview.tsx:114 uses text-emerald-500 where every other success indicator uses text-[hsl(var(--success))].
findings.impact: Four badge variants render the same colour in both themes, and the variant names (info/success/warning/error) form a second severity vocabulary competing with the real one.
findings.recommendation: Move the four variants onto --success, --warning and --destructive tokens. Fix badge-preview.tsx:114. Remove the dead --surface-* and --sidebar-* declarations.
